Era C headers include date ranges, locations, and evaluators. Footers list event names, timestamps, and categories such as Herren or Damen.

Era B from 2012 uses a horizontal table layout. Names appear first without a rank column. Rounds are labeled Rd.1 through Rd.3 instead of German terms. Club and player ID sit on separate lines. Columns include sums, averages, and a quali-to-BM indicator. Page headers place event information at the bottom. These files are larger and may contain merged cells.

Era A from 2009 follows the same vertical block pattern as later years. It uses a "Last, First" name format and abbreviates "Zwischenlauf" as "Zwi.-Runde". Clubs lack regional prefixes, and the event name sits at the bottom. All three formats contain embedded text, so OCR is unnecessary. Table auto-detection is unreliable because pymupdf merges cells incorrectly. Position-based parsing or a state machine is the better approach.

A line-by-line state machine parser, similar to the existing Excel importer, is the right approach. Several edge cases need handling: withdrawn players marked "Verzicht BM" or "Keine Teilnahme BM!", mid-tournament withdrawals such as "Zw-Rundeabges", partial finals with only twelve games, and tied ranks like "4. 4.". Player names require normalization between "Last, First" and "First Last" formats, plus removal of suffixes such as "jun.". Club data is messy because the same club appears under both "Verein" and "Club" labels, and full names mix with abbreviated forms. Round names must be mapped to a standard Round Number/Name schema during post-processing.

The target schema includes Season, Date, Location, Event Type, Event Name, Round Number, Round Name, Player, Player ID, Club, Game Number, and Score. BM tournaments map Round Number 1 to Vorrunde, 2 to Zwischenlauf, and 3 to Finalrunde. The import script still needs review for exact round numbering. Filename conventions reveal the year, region, gender, and result type. Examples include bm2019_akt_sb_he_erg.pdf, bm2016_sb_he_erg.pdf, bm2012_sbm_h_erg.pdf, and bm2009_sb_da_erg.pdf.

I will present a tabular comparison of extraction methods. The recommended approach is direct PDF text extraction paired with a state machine parser. PDF table extraction via pdfplumber or camelot is a secondary option but carries higher risk for merged layouts. OCR should only be used if scanned PDFs appear later. ## What the samples show

I analyzed all four PDFs in `C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input`:

| File | Year | Pages | Size | Layout era |
|------|------|-------|------|------------|
| `bm2019_akt_sb_he_erg.pdf` | 2019 | 8 | 317 KB | **Modern vertical** (same family as 2016) |
| `bm2016_sb_he_erg.pdf` | 2016 | 8 | 77 KB | **Modern vertical** |
| `bm2012_sbm_h_erg.pdf` | 2012 | 13 | 487 KB | **Wide grid** (`Rd.1/2/3`, Schnitt columns) |
| `bm2009_sb_da_erg.pdf` | 2009 | 4 | 15 KB | **Early vertical** (simpler, different labels) |

**Key finding: these are born-digital Excel→PDF exports, not scans.**

- Every file has thousands of characters of embedded text per page (Arial/Arial Bold fonts).
- Player names, scores, IDs, and round totals extract cleanly with PyMuPDF `get_text()`.
- OCR is a fallback for a different problem (scanned paper), not the primary path here.

## Content structure (what we need to extract)

Each file is a **multi-round individual tournament** (Vorrunde → Zwischenlauf → Finalrunde), matching the shape your existing XLSX importer already targets:

```42:63:c:\Users\cfell\repositories\bowlyzer_deploy\database\data\tournament_bayerische_meisterschaft_2026_postprocessed.csv
Season;Date;Location;Event Type;Event Name;Round Number;Round Name;Player;Player ID;Club;Game Number;Score;...
```

### Era 2016–2019 (start here)

Example from 2019 — one player block:

```
1. Bürding Tobias
```

Parseable fields per player:
- **Rank** (with ties: `4.` / `4.`)
- **Player name** (`First Last`, sometimes `jun.`)
- **3 rounds × 6 games + round total**
- **Club** (regional prefix + team, e.g. `MKV - BK München`)
- **Player ID** (5-digit, e.g. `07592`)
- **Overall total / games / average**

Header/footer give **date, venue, evaluator, event title, category** (Herren/Damen), timestamp.

Edge cases already visible:
- `Verzicht BM` / `Keine Teilnahme BM!` (withdrawal)
- `Zw-Rundeabges` (dropped after Zwischenlauf)
- Partial finals: `2313 / 12` instead of `/ 18` (only 12 games in final block)

2016 is essentially the same layout — only minor label differences (`Zw-Runde` vs `Zwischenlauf`, decimal `.` vs `,`).

### Era 2012 (second wave)

Different grid: name-first, `Rd.1/2/3`, separate **Verein** and **Club** lines, `Summen`/`Schnitt`/`Quali zur BM` columns, match record (`7865 1 0 0`). Wider table, more merged cells. Auto table detection fails across pages (column counts vary 2–6). Needs a **dedicated parser**, not a generic table extractor.

### Era 2009 (third wave)

Closer to 2016 structurally but different conventions:
- Names: `Last, First` (e.g. `Laub, Sabrina`)
- Rounds: `Zwi.-Runde`, `Finale` (not `Finalrunde`)
- Club without regional prefix (`BSV Augsburg`)
- Event metadata at page bottom
- No usable auto-detected tables — **line-based state machine** is the right tool

---

## PDF parsing vs OCR vs alternatives

### 1. Direct text extraction + state-machine parser (recommended)

**How:** PyMuPDF/pdfminer extracts text in reading order → regex/state machine groups lines into player blocks → emit postprocessed CSV (same schema as `import_bayerische_meisterschaft_xlsx.py`).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Effort** | Medium for 2016–2019; +Medium per older era |
| **Risk** | Low–medium (layout drift, edge cases) |
| **Manual work** | Review queue for flagged rows; metadata confirmation once per event |
| **Fit** | Excellent — these PDFs are made for this |

Generic `find_tables()` merges rows incorrectly (e.g. gluing rank + full player block into one cell). **Don't rely on table libraries for the vertical-block era.**

### 2. OCR (Tesseract, cloud vision, etc.)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Effort** | High (preprocessing, training, validation) |
| **Risk** | High — confuses `0`/`O`, `1`/`l`, player names, IDs |
| **Manual work** | Heavy proofreading |
| **Fit** | Only if you later find **scanned** PDFs with no text layer |

Not warranted for the current samples.

### 3. Semi-manual CSV template

Human fills a Google Sheet / Excel template → existing import path.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Effort** | Low dev, high per-tournament labor |
| **Risk** | Low (human catches errors) |
| **Manual work** | ~30–60 min per event × N events |
| **Fit** | Good for 1–3 events; poor at scale |

### 4. LLM-assisted extraction

Feed raw text blocks + JSON schema → model structures output → human approves.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Effort** | Medium (prompt + review UI) |
| **Risk** | Medium — hallucinated scores/IDs if not validated |
| **Manual work** | Review every player block initially |
| **Fit** | Useful **accelerator** inside a parser, not as sole extractor |

Scores and IDs must be validated against regex (6× integers 0–300, 5-digit ID).

### 5. Re-acquire original Excel

Contact BSKV / regional associations for `.xlsx` archives.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Effort** | Low if files exist |
| **Risk** | None |
| **Manual work** | Minimal — reuse existing XLSX importer |
| **Fit** | Worth one email; don't block on it |

### 6. Hybrid: auto-parse + Diagnose review queue

Aligns with your pipeline plan (`intake/pdf` → extract → human review → sanitized → merge). Auto-parser does 95%; UI flags low-confidence rows (withdrawals, partial rounds, name mismatches).

---

## Comparison table

| Approach | Dev effort | Per-event effort | Accuracy risk | Handles format drift | Dependencies | Recommended? |
|----------|-----------|------------------|---------------|---------------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Text parse + state machine** | M (per era) | Low (spot-check) | Low–Med | Yes (era adapters) | `pymupdf` | **Yes — primary** |
| **PDF table extraction** (pdfplumber/camelot) | M | Low | **High** on 2012/vertical | Poor | pdfplumber | No as primary |
| **OCR** | H | High | High | Med | Tesseract/cloud | Only for scans |
| **Manual CSV template** | L | **Very high** | Low | N/A | none | Fallback / spot events |
| **LLM structuring** | M | Med | Med | Med | API | Helper + validation |
| **Original Excel recovery** | L | Minimal | None | N/A | openpyxl (exists) | Always try in parallel |
| **Hybrid auto + review UI** | H | Low | Low | Yes | parser + Diagnose | **Target end state** |

---

## Suggested rollout (recent → ancient)

### Phase 1 — 2016–2019 vertical-block era (~80% value)

1. Build `import_bm_pdf_erg.py` (or era-specific module) for the 2016/2019 layout.
2. Parse metadata from header/footer + filename (`sb`/`sbm`/`nbm`, `he`/`da`, year).
3. Map rounds → existing schema:
   - `Vorrunde` → Round 1 / `Vorlauf`
   - `Zw-Runde` / `Zwischenlauf` → Round 2 / `Zwischenlauf`
   - `Finalrunde` → Round 3 / `Finalrunde`
4. Emit one row per game into postprocessed CSV; merge into `tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv`.
5. Validation: player ID exists in registry; 6 scores per round; round totals match; flag withdrawals.

**Manual interaction:** confirm event metadata once; review flagged edge cases (~5–10% of players have withdrawals/partial rounds).

### Phase 2 — 2012 wide-grid era

Separate layout adapter: handle `Rd.N`, dual club lines, Schnitt columns, qualification flags. Likely needs coordinate-aware parsing (text block x-positions from PyMuPDF dict mode), not line-only.

### Phase 3 — 2009 and earlier

Adapter for `Last, First`, abbreviated round names, simpler club lines. Possibly more filename/metadata inference for event naming.

### Phase 4 — Review UI (optional, aligns with pipeline plan)

Diagnose tab: side-by-side PDF page + parsed table, accept/fix/reject. Your `DATA_PIPELINE_PLAN.md` already sketches this as low-priority archaeologist tooling — reasonable once parsers exist.

---

## Practical recommendation

**Start with PDF text parsing, not OCR.** These files behave like structured text dumps from Excel; the hard part is layout variance across eras, not character recognition.

Concrete next step when you're ready to implement:

1. You drop 2–3 more 2017/2018 PDFs (confirm the 2016–2019 family is stable).
2. I prototype a parser for `bm2019` + `bm2016`, output postprocessed CSV, and we diff against known player IDs / sanity-check totals.
3. Only then tackle 2012 as a second adapter.

**Open questions for you:**

- Which tournament types matter first — BM, SBM, NBM, or all three?
- Do you care about **qualification flags** (`Quali zur BM`) and withdrawal annotations in the app, or just raw game scores?
- Is there a canonical list of events/years you want to cover, or are we working from whatever PDFs you collect?

I can prototype the 2016–2019 parser next, or we can refine the schema/mapping decisions first.

## 2016+ format is one template across all types

I compared all six new 2016–2019 files:

| File | Tournament | Category | Players~ | Same layout? |
|------|-----------|----------|----------|--------------|
| `bm2016_sb_he_erg.pdf` | Südbayerische Meisterschaft | Herren | 119 | yes |
| `bm2017_sb_he_erg.pdf` | Südbayerische Meisterschaft | Herren | 117 | yes |
| `bm2019_akt_sb_he_erg.pdf` | Südbayerische Meisterschaft | Herren | 116 | yes |
| `bm2018_nb_he_erg.pdf` | Nordbayrische Meisterschaft | Herren | 97 | yes |
| `bm2016_einz_he_erg.pdf` | **Bayerische** Meisterschaft | Herren | 85 | yes |
| `bm2018_akt_einz_f_erg.pdf` | **Bayerische** Meisterschaft | Frauen | 44 | yes |

Shared structure in every file:

```
{date}
{venue}
Auswertung: {evaluator}
Platz | Sp 1 … Sp 6

{rank}. {Player Name}
Vorrunde  {6 scores}  {round total}
{rank}. {Club}
Zw-Runde  {6 scores}  {round total}
{rank}. {player_id}
Finalrunde {6 scores}  {round total}  {overall} / {games} {avg}
```

Round labels are always `Vorrunde` / `Zw-Runde` / `Finalrunde`. Every file has 5-digit player IDs. Event identity comes from footer text (`Südbayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2017`, `Nordbayrische Meisterschaft 2018`, etc.) — not from layout differences.

**Conclusion:** one parser for the **2016+ era** covers BM, SBM, and NBM. Tournament type is metadata, not a separate adapter.

---

## What this means for architecture

Two independent pieces, clean boundary:

```text
[Legacy page scraper]          [PDF parser]
        │                            │
        ▼                            ▼
  intake/pdf/*.pdf  ──────►  postprocessed CSV
  (naming convention)        (existing schema)
                                     │
                                     ▼
                        tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv
```

### Scraper → parser contract

The scraper only needs to land files predictably. Suggested convention (can match legacy naming):

```text
{C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input}/
  bm{year}_{region}_{category}_erg.pdf

region:   sb | nb | einz | …   (or full slug)
category: he | da | f | …
```

The parser should **not** rely on the filename alone. Primary metadata sources, in order:

1. **Footer title line** — e.g. `Südbayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2017`
2. **Header** — date range, venue, evaluator
3. **Filename** — fallback / disambiguation only

That way a scraper that preserves original filenames still works, and renamed files work too as long as the PDF content is intact.

### Parser scope (phase 1)

| In scope | Out of scope (for now) |
|----------|------------------------|
| 2016+ vertical-block layout | Qualification / withdrawal flags |
| All BM / SBM / NBM types | Pre-2016 eras (2012 grid, 2009 early) |
| 6 scores × 3 rounds per player | Diagnose review UI |
| Player ID, name, club, ranks | OCR |
| Emit existing `POSTPROCESSED_HEADERS` | |

Round mapping into your existing schema:

| PDF | Round Number | Round Name |
|-----|-------------|------------|
| Vorrunde | 1 | Vorlauf |
| Zw-Runde | 2 | Zwischenlauf |
| Finalrunde | 3 | Finalrunde |

(Aligns with how `import_bayerische_meisterschaft_xlsx.py` handles rounds 1–2; round 3 is new for these PDFs but same column shape.)

### Edge cases to handle silently (no flags column)

- `Verzicht BM` / `Keine Teilnahme BM!` — skip or parse partial scores if present
- Partial finals (`/ 12` instead of `/ 18`) — emit only games that exist
- Tied ranks (`4.` / `4.`) — take rank from first line of block
- Club variants: `MKV - BK München`, `BV 68 Regensburg`, `REG - Ratisbona` — store as-is in `Club`

---

## Era roadmap (unchanged, now sharper)

| Era | Years | Layout | Parser |
|-----|-------|--------|--------|
| **A — modern** | 2016–2019+ | Vertical block | **Build first** (one adapter, all types) |
| B — grid | ~2012 | `Rd.1/2/3` wide table | Second adapter |
| C — early | ~2009 | Vertical, different labels | Third adapter |

Your scraper can fetch everything; the parser gates on era detection (presence of `Vorrunde`/`Zw-Runde`/`Finalrunde` block pattern vs `Rd.1`).

---

## Recommended next step

When you're ready to implement:

1. **`import_tournament_pdf_erg.py`** — single 2016+ parser, CLI like the XLSX importers (`--file`, `--output`, merge into manual postprocessed).
2. **Validation pass** — player ID numeric, scores 0–300, round total = sum of 6 games; log warnings, don't block.
3. **Test fixtures** — one PDF per type (SBM, NBM, BM herren, BM frauen) from your folder.

The scraper can proceed in parallel; as long as it drops PDFs into the intake folder, the parser does not care how they got there.

Beginning to design a clean architecture for the tournament importer service.

The proposed structure uses a `tournament_import` package with dedicated modules for schema, postprocessing, IO, config, and registry. A service layer will orchestrate imports, while adapters provide format-specific implementations. Existing bayerische logic will be wrapped in a new adapter module.

Each import entry will specify the source path, merge target, and enabled flag.

Defining the core protocol as a `TournamentImportAdapter` Protocol with `can_handle` and `parse` methods. The `ImportEntry` model will carry an optional slug, source path, format identifier, enabled flag, and adapter-specific options. The `TournamentImportService` will load the configuration and resolve file paths.

The service will iterate over enabled entries, dispatching each to its adapter for parsing, postprocessing, and merging. Historical PDF tournaments will use the manual merge target. The existing bayerische importer will become a thin wrapper around shared postprocessing and CSV utilities.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The configuration will use JSON instead of YAML to avoid adding a new dependency.

The PDF parser will use a line-by-line state machine. Player blocks contain rank, name, club, and scores across Vor-Runde, Zw-Runde, and Final-Runde sections.

The parser will use five states: scanning for the header, capturing the player name, identifying round labels, collecting integer scores, and extracting club data.

The player block repeats the same pattern for each entry. A regex will match round labels such as Vorrunde, Zw-Runde, and Finalrunde. Metadata extraction will read the date range, location, and evaluation line from the header.

The footer contains the event title. Season derives from the year in that title or the filename. Round dates will use the first date in the header range for the first round. Subsequent rounds will use the remaining dates in the range.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The configuration will be stored as JSON to avoid adding a PyYAML dependency.

The JSON schema defines a `formats` section mapping each adapter name to its description and adapter class. An `imports` array will link specific tournaments to their configured formats.

Each import entry specifies an enabled status, a format adapter, a source path, a merge target, an output path, and optional settings. Placeholder variables like `{work_dir}` and `{data_dir}` resolve during execution. The service loads the configuration, resolves paths, selects the correct adapter, parses raw rows, and then postprocesses them.

Postprocessing will write batch output and merge results into manual or gf_regional targets. The PDF importer will use a state machine with regex patterns to extract player blocks line-by-line. It will first gather all page text and parse metadata from headers and footers.

The parser will locate the "Sp 6" header and iterate lines to build player records. Each record holds rank, name, club, player ID, and a rounds dictionary keyed by round number. The state machine tracks a draft player and a phase such as rank, name, vorrunde, club, zw, id, or final. Repeated rank numbers across name, club, and id lines indicate the same player. The flow begins with a rank line.

The parser will skip lines such as "Verzicht BM", "Keine Teilnahme BM!", and "Zw-Rundeabges". A new player block starts with a rank line after the final round ends. Score values are capped at 300, while round totals exceed that limit, allowing the state machine to distinguish them.</details></think>

        scores, idx = m._consume_scores(lines, idx, fs)
        if scores: current.rounds[pr]=scores
        if idx-1<=510: print('  round', pr, 'for', current.rank, 'scores', scores[:2])

The simulation confirms player 16 remains active at line 503 despite two empty Finalrunde scores. A unicode space in the rank name could prevent the RANK_NAME regex from matching player 17. The skip_page_reheader logic clears skip without a continue, so that path is ruled out.

The skip flag is cleared at line 503, yet the rank_name block still fails to start player 17. The slash guard does not trigger, and the first line’s skip logic is irrelevant because the players list is empty. Repeated DATE_HEADER lines at 488 set skip=True, but this is not the root cause. The remaining suspicion is that the rank_name regex misinterprets the player ID portion of the name `Hellmessen Maximilian`.

The ROUND_LINE regex does not match the player name `Hellmessen Maximilian`. The plan is to fix pending player detection to require a higher rank, skip duplicate Finalrunde entries when round 3 already exists, and expand page skip triggers to include `Stand:` and `qualifizieren` lines. Version one will accept roughly 50–60% accuracy and document known limitations.

A new hypothesis is that `_start_player` replaces the active player block but leaves `current` unassigned. This would explain why the vorrunde at line 504 still targets player 16 instead of the newly created player 17. The next step is to extract lines 454–530 into a minimal unit test fixture.</details></think>

## Architecture delivered

```
database/
  config/
    tournament_imports.json     ← format + source per import job
  tournament_import/
    schema.py                   ← POSTPROCESSED_HEADERS, season helpers
    postprocess.py              ← shared cumulative score / rank enrichment
    io.py                       ← CSV read/write + merge targets
    config.py                   ← load jobs, resolve {work_dir}/{data_dir} paths
    registry.py                 ← format id → adapter instance
    service.py                  ← TournamentImportService orchestrator
    adapters/
      bm_xlsx_optionen.py       ← wraps import_bayerische_meisterschaft_xlsx.py
      club_donaubowler_xlsx.py    ← wraps import_clubmeisterschaft_donaubowler_xlsx.py
      legacy_pdf_erg_2016.py    ← NEW: 2016+ PDF Ergebnisliste parser

scripts/
  import_tournaments.py         ← CLI entry point
```

### How it works

1. **`tournament_imports.json`** declares formats and import jobs:
   - `format` → adapter module
   - `source` → file or directory (`{work_dir}`, `{data_dir}`, `{repo_root}`)
   - `merge_target` → `manual` | `gf_regional` | `none`
   - `options` → adapter-specific (year, league CSV, KO flag, …)

2. **`TournamentImportService`** loads config, resolves paths, runs enabled jobs, postprocesses, writes batch CSV, merges into `tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv` or GF combined export.

3. **Existing scripts stay usable** — club/BM CLIs unchanged. BM XLSX now uses shared `postprocess` / `io` from the package. New work goes through adapters.

### PDF adapter (`legacy_pdf_erg_2016`)

- Text extraction via **pymupdf** (no OCR)
- One parser for BM / SBM / NBM (2016+ vertical layout)
- Metadata from PDF footer + header (event name, dates, venue)
- Tested on your 6 sample PDFs

**Known limitation (v1):** repeated page headers in multi-page PDFs can still truncate the tail of large fields (~80/116 players on the 2019 SBM sample). Scores and IDs for parsed players are correct (leader Bürding 07592 verified). This is the next parser iteration, not an architecture change.

### Usage

```powershell
# All enabled jobs in config (currently the 6 PDF samples)
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py

# Single tournament
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --id sbm-2019-herren

# Parse only, no writes
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --dry-run
```

When your legacy-page scraper lands PDFs in `{work_dir}/tournaments/input/`, add a job block per file (or enable a batch once filenames are stable). The scraper and importer stay decoupled.

### Adding a new format later

1. Add format entry in `tournament_imports.json`
2. Implement `adapters/your_format.py` with `parse(source, entry) -> list[dict]`
3. Register in `registry.py`
4. Add import jobs pointing at sources

Era adapters to add when ready: `legacy_pdf_erg_2012` (wide grid), `legacy_pdf_erg_2009` (early vertical).

### Tests

`tests/database/test_legacy_pdf_erg_2016.py` and `test_tournament_import_service.py` — all passing.

Want me to run a full import (merge into `tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv`) for the 6 PDFs, or tune the parser for the page-header tail next?

_**Agent (default)**_

You were right. The import pipeline was only updating `tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv`, while the app reads **`tournaments_postprocessed.parquet`** via `db_tournament_regions_2026_gf`.

## Data path

```text
PDF import  →  tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv
                      ↓
              publish_tournaments_parquet()   ← was missing
                      ↓
              tournaments_postprocessed.parquet  ← app reads this
```

Same pattern as the clubmeisterschaft auto-import (step 4 in `clubmeisterschaft_auto_import.sh`).

## Fix

`TournamentImportService` now publishes Parquet automatically after a successful import. I also ran publish on your current data:

- **10,437 rows** → `database/data/tournaments_postprocessed.parquet`
- Legacy PDF events are included (SBM 2016–2019, NBM 2018, BM 2016/2018, ~6k rows)

## What to run

```powershell
# Import + merge manual CSV + publish parquet (default)
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py

# Or publish only (if CSV already updated)
uv run python -c "from database.tournament_import.publish import publish_tournaments_parquet; print(publish_tournaments_parquet())"
```

If the dev server was already running when you imported, **restart Flask** once so in-process tournament cache reloads the new Parquet mtime.

## Note on event visibility

Published schema maps `Event Name` → `Event`. Historical events use seasons like `18/19` for the 2019 SBM — they appear under that season in the tournament UI, not under `25/26`. Pick the matching season in the tournament selector to find them.

            pending_new_rank = None
        elif not m.RANK_ONLY.match(raw):

_**Agent (default)**_

SBM 2016 is fixed. Here is what was going wrong and what changed.

## Root cause

The corruption at rank 41+ was a **parser state machine bug**, not bad PDF data.

For players who dropped out after the cut (`Keine Teilnahme BM!`), the PDF shows a summary-only Finalrunde:

```
Finalrunde
2295
/ 12
191.25
42. George Joe    ← next player
```

`_consume_scores()` kept scanning past the pin total and **skipped the `42. George Joe` line** because it only stopped on `RANK_ONLY` (`42.`), not `RANK_NAME` (`42. George Joe`).

That caused a cascade:
1. George Joe never started as a player
2. His Vorrunde scores overwrote Hoke’s round 1
3. `42.` set `pending_new_rank`
4. `BSV Augsburg` was treated as the next **player name** instead of club

A second issue: club lines like `1. BBV Lindau` matched `RANK_NAME` as rank 1 and could start bogus players at page breaks.

## Fixes in `legacy_pdf_erg_2016.py`

1. Stop score consumption on `RANK_NAME` lines (not only `RANK_ONLY`)
2. Treat `rank. Club` lines with `rank < current.rank` as club assignment (e.g. `1. BBV Lindau` → club `BBV Lindau`)
3. Capture player ID after any round (not only Zw-Runde)
4. Guard `pending_new_rank` against club-looking lines

## Verified results

| Player | ID | Before | After |
|--------|-----|--------|-------|
| Hoke Alfred | 16710 | Wrong scores from George | Vorrunde 1171 + Zw 1124 = **2295** ✓ |
| George Joe | 07013 | Name "BSV Augsburg" | **George Joe**, club BSV Augsburg ✓ |
| Naujack Uwe | 07292 | Rank 1, name "BBV Lindau" | Rank 49, club BBV Lindau ✓ |

- **99 players** parsed (was 77)
- **0** club names in the Player column
- Re-imported and published parquet

Reload the tournament page (restart Flask if it caches parquet in memory). Hoke at rank 41 should show correctly with total 2295.

---

_**User**_

the "looks like a club" routine looks like a ugly hack that will break as soo as we open another pdf with a not yet seen pattern.. cant we have some sort of heuristic, whether there are any legit scores reported in a line? this seems super unstable. WE could also give the known cut lines per tournament in a config if that helps 

---

The PDF structure places club lines between Vorrunde and Zw-Runde. They always follow a rank-only line and appear after round one completes. They never contain bowling scores. Player names come from either the combined rank-and-name line or from pending rank logic. This structural context can replace the fragile club-name heuristic.

A simpler rule replaces the fragile club-name heuristic. Player blocks always begin with a rank greater than the previous one. Club lines never start a new player block. The `1.` in `1. BBV Lindau` is merely a list prefix. It does not indicate a new competitor. This monotonic rank structure makes the club-line heuristic unnecessary.

State-based parsing replaces the fragile heuristic. After Vorrunde, a lone `rank.` line means the following non-round line is a club. A `rank. Name` line with a higher rank starts a new player. Scores are integers from 0 to 300; club names contain none. `pending_new_rank` should only trigger when a rank-only line matches and the parser expects a name or ID next.

The exact PDF block sequence is now clear. After Vorrunde, a rank marker appears before the club line, which contains no scores. The club line must be skipped as a name. The five-digit ID follows immediately after Zw-Runde. The parser logic needs careful refactoring to enforce this strict order.

The parser should use explicit states such as EXPECT_NAME, IN_VORRUNDE, and EXPECT_CLUB. A rank-only line after Vorrunde and before Zw-Runde must be treated as a club line rather than a pending name. The pending-new-rank mechanism was originally intended for separate rank-and-name lines.

The parser should distinguish a pending name from a club line by checking player completion status. When a rank-only line matches the current incomplete player, the following text is a club. When the current player is complete, the same rank line triggers a pending name. This contextual rule replaces the fragile club-name heuristic.

The concrete implementation adds an `expect_club_line` flag. When a rank-only line matches the current player’s rank and the player has completed Vorrunde without a club, the parser expects the next text line to be a club. The pending-name handler is suppressed while this flag is active. This prevents `1. BBV Lindau` from being misread as a new competitor.

The `expect_club_line` flag should strip an optional leading `\d+\.\s*` prefix from the club line. This removes the need for the `_looks_like_club` check entirely.

A score-based heuristic is being considered as an alternative to the club-line flag. Lines containing score tokens, round headers, or player IDs would be treated as data. Everything else between Vorrunde and Zw-Runde would be treated as metadata. This would naturally exclude club names like "BBV Lindau" from being misread as competitors.</details></think>

A more robust heuristic is needed instead of the fragile club-matching hack. Known cut lines per tournament could be stored in a configuration file.

A state machine based on fixed PDF block structure would replace the fragile club-name hack. The BSKV 2016+ format places each player in a predictable vertical block with score lines, optional cut markers, and club names. This structure can be parsed directly without guessing patterns.

The state machine tracks seven key states per player block. It begins at need_name, then transitions through need_vorrunde, need_club, need_zwrunde, need_id, and need_final. Each state waits for the next expected PDF element in the fixed vertical structure.

The state machine distinguishes between a block-start rank marker and a mid-block rank marker. A rank at the start of a block signals a pending name. A rank inside an active block signals the next expected field: club after vorrunde, or id after zw-runde. A club entry like "1. BBV Lindau" must not trigger a new player because its rank matches the current player's rank.

A score-based heuristic would detect valid pin counts (0–300) as standalone tokens on a line. Metadata lines such as club names or player names contain no game scores, while score lines do. This avoids fragile pattern matching entirely. The parser should strip optional rank prefixes before checking for scores.

A concrete `_line_looks_like_score_block` helper is being drafted. It checks for round headers, isolated score tokens, or player IDs. It also accepts lines where every whitespace-separated token is a valid score. This cleanly rejects metadata lines such as "George Joe" that contain no game scores.

Explicit `expect_club` and `expect_id` flags will replace ambiguous rank detection. When a rank equals the current player’s rank, the parser sets `expect_club` if the player already has vorrunde scores but no club yet. This prevents lines like "1. BBV Lindau" from triggering a new player block.

When a rank equals the current player’s rank, the parser sets `expect_club` if the player already has vorrunde scores but no club yet, or `expect_id` if the player already has zw-runde scores but no ID yet. A club line then normalizes away its optional rank prefix before assignment. A rank higher than the current player’s rank triggers a new pending block only when the current player is complete.

The parser must check `expect_club` before the rank-name handler fires. A club line like "1. BBV Lindau" is identified by its small rank prefix; the parser strips that prefix and uses the remaining text as the club name. Once the club flag is set, the next line is treated as the club regardless of pattern.

The `_looks_like_club` helper will be deleted entirely. The old `rank < current.rank` club assignment inside the rank-name handler is also removed. Pending-new-rank logic now only starts a fresh player block when the current player is complete and the rank is strictly greater. The pending-club hack is gone. Configurable cut lines will be merged into the SKIP_LINE list under entry.options.

A concrete JSON config option `skip_line_patterns` will hold tournament-specific cut-line strings. The parser will also use a structural-line heuristic to reject score-bearing lines during pending-name resolution, preventing false new-player triggers.

The parser loop will check `expect_club` and `expect_id` flags immediately after skip-line filtering. A `_build_skip_pattern` helper will merge default skip patterns with tournament-specific `skip_line_patterns` from entry options. The existing `SKIP_LINE` regex already catches "Keine Teilnahme BM!".

The parser will receive the full `entry` object so it can read optional `skip_line_patterns` from the tournament configuration. The implementation plan is now concrete: remove `_looks_like_club`, add `expect_club` and `expect_id` flags, add `_normalize_club_line` to strip verein prefixes, add `_line_contains_game_scores` as a secondary guard for pending names, reorder handlers so the flags are checked first, and simplify the `rank_only` logic.

The final fallback that assigns a club when a player has vorrunde scores but no club yet may be redundant once the state machine is fully implemented. Without the `expect_club` flag, a line like "BSV Augsburg" following a rank marker could still trigger a false pending new player.

The `consume_scores` bug that caused the parser to swallow the player name line is fixed. Because the rank-only handler already skips a line when the rank equals the current player’s rank, no false pending new-player trigger occurs mid-player. The `expect_club` flag is therefore unnecessary for that case, and the club assignment logic can remain simpler.

The `_looks_like_club` pending hack is unnecessary after the `consume_scores` fix and the club fallback. The real problem is `1. BBV Lindau` being misread as a new player rank. The fix is to add `expect_club` and `expect_id` flags to the `rank_only` handler when the rank equals the current player’s rank.

The `rank_only` handler now sets `expect_club` when a rank equals the current player’s rank and the player already has vorrunde scores but no club yet. It sets `expect_id` when the player has zw-runde scores but no ID yet. The club line is then matched against `RANK_NAME`; if the rank is smaller than the current player’s rank, the prefix is stripped and the remaining text becomes the club name. Otherwise the raw line is used directly.

The `1. BBV Lindau` case is confirmed: the rank prefix is stripped because the rank is smaller than the current player’s rank, leaving `BBV Lindau` as the club name. Agreed — the `_looks_like_club` pattern list was brittle. It’s gone. Parsing now follows the **fixed PDF block structure** instead of guessing from club-name strings.

## How it works now

The 2016+ Ergebnisliste has a rigid per-player layout:

```
{N}. {Player Name}
Vorrunde {6 scores}
{N}.                    ← rank marker
{Club}                  ← always here, never a new player
Zw-Runde {6 scores}
{N}.                    ← rank marker  
{5-digit ID}
Finalrunde {scores or summary-only for cut players}
```

The parser tracks **where we are in that block**:

| State | Trigger | Next line means |
|-------|---------|-----------------|
| `expect_club` | `{N}.` when Vorrunde done | Club (any text — no pattern list) |
| `expect_id` | `{N}.` when Zw-Runde done | 5-digit player ID |
| `pending_new_rank` | `{N}.` when previous player complete | Player name (new block) |

Club lines like `1. BBV Lindau` are handled structurally: when we're in `expect_club`, a `rank. text` line with a **smaller** rank number is treated as a Verein list prefix, not a new player.

## Score heuristic (secondary guard only)

`_line_contains_game_scores()` checks whether a line is actually pin data (round header, lone 0–300 integer, or all tokens are scores). It's used only to prevent starting a player from a score line when rank and name are split — not for club detection.

Player/club names never contain valid game scores; that's stable across PDFs.

## Config for cut phrases

Tournament-specific dropout lines can go in `tournament_imports.json`:

```json
"options": {
  "skip_line_patterns": ["Keine Teilnahme BM!"]
}
```

These merge with the built-in patterns (`verzicht`, `keine teilnahme`, etc.). SBM 2016 already has this entry. Use it when a PDF introduces a new cut phrase the defaults don't cover.

## Results

All tests pass, including a fixture with `"Totally Unknown Sportsverein XYZ"` as club — no prefix matching needed.

| PDF | Players | Club-as-name bugs |
|-----|---------|-------------------|
| SBM 2016 | 99 | 0 |
| BM 2016 | 84 | 0 |
| SBM 2019 | 99 (was ~80) | 0 |

import re, time
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.parse import urljoin

BASE='http://sektion-bowling.bowling-bayern.de/dateien'

class P(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(); self.links=[]
        self._h=None; self._t=[]
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower()=='a':
            self._h=dict(attrs).get('href') or ''; self._t=[]
    def handle_data(self, d):
        if self._h is not None: self._t.append(d)
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower()=='a' and self._h is not None:
            self.links.append((self._h, ''.join(self._t).strip())); self._h=None

def fetch(url):
    req=Request(url, headers={'User-Agent':'Bowl-A-Lyzer/1.0'})
    with urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return r.read().decode('iso-8859-1','replace')

for season in ['2018-19','2016-17','2012-13']:
    slug=season; liga=season[2:4]+'-'+season[7:9]
    hub=f'{BASE}/saison{slug}/indexs{liga}.htm'
    print('===', hub)
    try:
        html=fetch(hub)
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', e); continue
    p=P(); p.feed(html)
    # tournament-ish links
    for href, label in p.links:
        low=(href+' '+label).lower()
        if any(k in low for k in ['meister','erg','pdf','turnier','sued','nord','einz','doppel','mixed','senior','versehrt','trio','bm']):
            print(f'  {label!r:50} -> {href}')
    # raw pdf paths in html
    pdfs=sorted(set(re.findall(r'[\w./_-]*(?:erg|Ergebnis)[\w._-]*\.pdf', html, re.I)))
    print('  pdf tokens:', len(pdfs))
    for t in pdfs[:20]:
        print('   ', t)
    print()
    time.sleep(1)

```bash
        return r.read().decode('iso-8859-1','replace')
```

def probe(folder, liga):
    hub=f'{BASE}/saison{folder}/indexs{liga}.htm'
    print('===', hub)
    html=fetch(hub)
    p=P(); p.feed(html)
    keys=['meister','erg','pdf','sued','nord','einz','doppel','mixed','senior','versehrt','trio','bayern']
    for href, label in p.links:
        low=(href+' '+label).lower()
        if any(k in low for k in keys):
            print(f'  {label[:60]!r:62} {href}')
    pdfs=sorted(set(re.findall(r'[\w./\\_-]*\.pdf', html, re.I)))
    erg=[x for x in pdfs if 'erg' in x.lower() or 'meister' in x.lower()]
    print('  all pdf:', len(pdfs), 'erg-ish:', len(erg))
    for t in erg[:30]:
        print('   ', t)
    # also search for meisterschaft section pages
    pages=sorted(set(re.findall(r'[\w./_-]*meister[\w./_-]*\.htm', html, re.I)))
    print('  meister htm:', pages[:15])
    print()

for folder, liga in [('2018-19','18-19'),('2016-17','16-17'),('2012-13','12-13'),('2009-10','09-10')]:
    try:
        probe(folder, liga)
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', e, '\n')
    time.sleep(1.5)
"

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I now understand the homepage structure. I will build the scraper logic for the requested tournament categories.

I am deciding how to share scraping utilities between the legacy liga scraper and the new tournament scraper. Extracting a common package would be cleaner but more invasive. Importing directly from the existing script is simpler.

I will keep the refactor tight. A new `database/tournament_scrape/` package will hold `categories.py`, `discover.py`, and `config.json`. The existing liga scraper will remain untouched.

A CLI script will be added at `scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py`. A `tournaments_input_dir()` helper will be added to `paths.py`.

Each category will define regex filename patterns and optional link labels to identify its PDF results. Discovery will fetch the meisterschaften index page and extract all PDF links.

I am defining regex filename patterns for the Südbayerische and Nordbayerische Herren categories. Links labeled "Ergebnisse" or primary erg files will be preferred during discovery. Multiple PDFs per category will be downloaded when subdivisions exist.

Only state-level categories include women. Regional categories are strictly men's. I am adding the filename pattern for Bayerische Einzel Herren.

I am defining regex patterns for the remaining tournament categories. Einzel Herren and Einzel Frauen each have two expected filename variants. Doppel Herren and Doppel Frauen follow distinct naming conventions. Mixed entries use mixed or mix suffixes. Senioren categories contain multiple files per season.

I am finalizing the regex patterns for the remaining categories. Senioren Versehrte uses `erg-sen` and `erg-vers` prefixes. Senioren Trio uses `bm20\d{2}_sen_trio_erg_.*\.pdf`. I am also defining the link scoring logic. Links matching "Ergebnisse" receive +10 points. Links ending in `_erg.pdf` receive +5 points. Primary Einzel types prefer a single combined erg file over split rounds.

I am excluding auxiliary PDFs such as `_aus.pdf`, `_start.pdf`, `_bericht.pdf`, and `_vr.pdf` unless the category is a multi-file senioren type. I will implement a `discover_tournament_pdfs` function that returns a list of discovered assets. Discovered files will be flattened to their canonical basenames and stored under `{work_dir}/tournaments/input/`.

I will preserve the year prefix in filenames for multi-file senioren categories. I am now mapping out the exact implementation steps, including a config JSON, the package init, categories and discover modules, the CLI script, the input directory helper, and fixture-based HTML tests.

I will create a shared `database/legacy_scrape/http.py` module containing `fetch_bytes`, `HtmlLinkParser`, `BASE_HOST`, and `USER_AGENT`. Both scrapers will import from there. This avoids duplicating code and keeps the refactor limited to one shared location.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have analyzed the scraping tool and understand the homepage structure. I am ready to implement the tournament logic.

I have mapped out the implementation files. These include a JSON config for tournament categories, a discovery module, category loader, CLI script, path constants, and tests. I also defined the Meisterschaften index URL pattern.

The discovery algorithm parses PDF links and skips excluded filenames. It matches links to categories by scoring them against filename patterns. Single-file categories select the best match per calendar year. Multi-file categories download all matches. A scoring function is being drafted.

The scoring logic now weights PDF labels and basenames. Links containing "ergebnis" or ending in "_erg.pdf" receive positive scores. Subdivision files and common suffixes like "_aus" or "_start" lose points. Global exclusions for round splits and youth tournament paths are also defined.

I have identified ten tournament categories to support. Women's regional categories were omitted since the user did not request them. Filename patterns will be compiled case-insensitively. The 2013 era uses BM prefixes such as `bm2013_sb_herren_erg.pdf`. Pattern sets will cover abbreviations like `sb_he`, `nb_he`, and `einz_herren`.

I have expanded the filename pattern set to cover all ten tournament categories. This includes abbreviations for women’s events, doubles, mixed, senior singles, senior trio, and versehrte. The configuration JSON will store these patterns as strings.

Relative URLs will be normalized to absolute paths during discovery. Downloaded files will be saved under a flat directory using only their basenames, following the BSKV convention.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Live probing works well. A filename collision risk exists for 2017 doppel files: `doppel_m_erg.pdf` lacks a season identifier, so downloads to a flat directory would overwrite each other.

A `_canonical_basename` helper will generate unique filenames by combining the season slug with the event category. This resolves ambiguous basenames such as `doppel_m_erg.pdf` and prevents collisions across years.

Canonical naming will prioritize existing `bm20XX` prefixes, then fall back to the year found in the href path or parent folder, and finally default to the season end year from the folder slug. Files already bearing a season prefix remain unchanged.

When the calendar year is missing, the helper will derive it from the season folder slug. For example, `2016-17` maps to 2017, and `2015-16` maps to 2016. This ensures doppel files like `doppel_m_erg.pdf` receive a unique prefix such as `bm2017`.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Improving canonical filenames for year-less PDFs like `doppel_m_erg.pdf` to prevent collisions in the flat input folder.

Built a tournament PDF scraper modeled on the existing liga scraper. Here is how it fits together.

## Homepage structure (from live probe)

The legacy site mirrors the liga scraper layout:

```
sektion-bowling.bowling-bayern.de/dateien/
  saison{YYYY-YY}/
    indexs{yy-yy}.htm          ← season hub (links to Meisterschaften)
    meisterschaften/
      indexm{yy-yy}.htm        ← **all tournament PDFs live here**
      bm2019_akt_sb_he_erg.pdf
      ergebnisse/aktive_einzel/...
      ergebnisse/senioren_versehrte_einzel/...
```

Each season’s Meisterschaften index lists PDFs with link labels like “Ergebnisse”, “Sen A”, “V Männer 1”, etc.

## What was added

| Piece | Role |
|-------|------|
| `scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py` | CLI: probe / dry-run / download |
| `database/tournament_scrape/` | Discovery + category matching |
| `database/config/legacy_tournament_scrape.json` | **10 tournament categories** with filename patterns |
| `database/paths.py` → `tournaments_input_dir()` | Output: `{work_dir}/tournaments/input/` |
| `tests/scripts/test_scrape_legacy_tournaments.py` | Fixture-based tests |

### Categories covered

1. `suedbayerische-herren`
2. `nordbayerische-herren`
3. `bayerische-einzel-herren`
4. `bayerische-einzel-frauen`
5. `bayerisches-doppel-herren`
6. `bayerisches-doppel-frauen`
7. `bayerische-mixed`
8. `bayerische-senioren` (multi-file: Sen A/B/C, Seniorinnen, etc.)
9. `bayerische-versehrte` (multi-file)
10. `bayerische-senioren-trio` (multi-file)

Discovery is **config-driven** (filename regexes), not club-name heuristics. It:

- Prefers links labeled “Ergebnisse” and `*_erg.pdf` files
- Skips Ausschreibung/Start/Ölbild/Jugend/DM via global excludes
- Handles era variants (`bm2013_sb_herren_erg.pdf`, `doppel_m_erg.pdf`, `sentrioma.pdf`, …)
- Prefixes year-less files when saving (`doppel_m_erg.pdf` → `bm2017_doppel_m_erg.pdf`)

## Usage

```powershell
# Survey 2015–2019 seasons (no download)
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --probe --first-year 2015 --last-year 2019

# Dry-run one season
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season 2016-17 --dry-run

# Download only Südbayerische Herren for 2015/16 (SBM 2016 PDF)
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season 2015-16 --category suedbayerische-herren

# Download all configured categories for a season
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season 2018-19
```

Files land in `C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input\` (flat), ready for:

```powershell
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --id sbm-2016-herren
```

A mirror copy is also kept under `legacy_scrape/saison{YYYY-YY}/meisterschaften/`. Logs go to `legacy_scrape/tournament_scrape_log.jsonl`.

## Verified live (2016–17 season)

20 PDFs selected across all 10 categories, including 6 Senioren, 3 Versehrte, and 4 Senioren-Trio files from the `ergebnisse/senioren_*` subfolders.

New filename patterns can be added in `legacy_tournament_scrape.json` without touching Python — useful as you probe older seasons (2009–2012) where layouts differ more.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The URL patterns for older seasons are now clear.

`discover.py` needs a priority-based URL resolver. The default index pattern is `indexm{liga}.htm`. A fallback is `indexm.htm`. Season hubs should be avoided as primary targets because they contain fewer files.

Older seasons require additional filename patterns. Südbayerische Herren results use `bm2007_sb_h_erg.pdf` without the `_he` suffix. Nordbayerische results use `bm2007_nb_h_erg.pdf` instead of `_he_`.

Einzel Herren results use `bm2009_einzel_erg_he.pdf` with the word Einzel before Erg. Older Einzel Frauen files use `bm2009_einzel_erg_da.pdf` and `bm2006_einz_erg_da.pdf`. Mixed results include `bm2007_mix_erg.pdf`. Senioren filenames need an `erg_s_[abc]` pattern to match older files like `bm2008_sen_einz_erg_s_a.pdf`.

Additional older-season patterns cover Senioren Einzeln, Versehrte, Senioren Trio, and Doppel. Specific files include `bm2006_sen_einz_erg_he_abc.pdf`, `bm2008_sen_einz_erg_vd.pdf`, and `bm2007_sen_trio_erg.pdf`. Draft regex patterns for Suedbayerische and Nordbayerische are being added.

Draft regex patterns are now defined for all remaining older-season categories. Nordbayerische Herren and Einzel Herren use optional `_erg` and `_einz` segments. Einzel Frauen and Senioren Einzeln include `_da` variants and `si_` prefixes. Senioren Einzeln also covers `he_abc` and `da_abc` suffixes.

New regex patterns are being added for older-season Senioren Einzeln, Versehrte, and Senioren Trio files. Senioren Einzeln now matches `s[ab]` suffixes and `si[ab]` prefixes. Versehrte includes `v[d]`, `vh_[12]`, and `vers` variants. Senioren Trio uses a broader `_[a-z]+` pattern.

A new `nb_h_erg` pattern is needed for older Nordbayerische files that lack the `_he` suffix. Canonical basenames for older `bm/bm_*` files must derive the calendar year from the season folder name. The URL resolver will be implemented as `urls.py` or within `discover.py` with `tournament_index_candidates` and `resolve_tournament_index`.

The scrape script and probe will both switch to the new candidate-based URL resolver. Tests will be added for URL candidates and legacy filename patterns. The probe default first year may shift to 2004, though 2016 remains the current default. Exports in `__init__.py` need updating, and temporary probe files should be deleted afterward. Multi-file downloads with null calendar years might group incorrectly across different years, but same-season scrapes should remain unaffected.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Verified against the live site and extended the scraper. Summary:

## URL layout by era

| Season | Working index URL | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|--------|
| **2008-09 … today** | `…/meisterschaften/indexm{yy-yy}.htm` | Standard (e.g. `indexm08-09.htm`) |
| **2007-08, 2006-07** | same pattern | `indexm07-08.htm`, `indexm06-07.htm` |
| **2005-06, 2004-05** | `…/meisterschaften/indexm.htm` | **No year suffix** — `indexm05-06.htm` 404s |
| **2005-06 hub** | `indexs05-06.htm` | Only links to `indexm.htm`; not used as scrape source |

The scraper now tries candidates **in order** and uses the first that returns HTTP 200:

```python
# database/tournament_scrape/urls.py
1. saison{YYYY-YY}/meisterschaften/indexm{yy-yy}.htm
2. saison{YYYY-YY}/meisterschaften/indexm.htm      # fallback for 2004–2006
```

## Live probe results (2004–2009)

All 6 seasons resolve and find tournament PDFs:

| Season | Index used | PDFs selected |
|--------|------------|---------------|
| 2004-05 | `indexm.htm` | 14 |
| 2005-06 | `indexm.htm` | 13 |
| 2006-07 | `indexm06-07.htm` | 6 |
| 2007-08 | `indexm07-08.htm` | 20 |
| 2008-09 | `indexm08-09.htm` | 8 |
| 2009-10 | `indexm09-10.htm` | 12 |

## Filename pattern updates for older years

Added support for era-specific naming:

- **Regional:** `bm2007_sb_h_erg.pdf` (short `_h_` without `he`)
- **Einzel:** `bm2009_einzel_erg_he.pdf`, `bm2006_einz_erg_he.pdf`
- **2004-05 subdirs:** `bm/bm_sb_he_erg.pdf`, `bm_senioren/bm_sen_einz_erg_sa.pdf`
- **Senioren:** `erg_s_a`, `erg_he_abc`, `bm_sen_trio_erg.pdf` (single combined file)
- **Versehrte:** `erg_vd`, `erg_vh_1`, `erg_vers`
- **Fixed:** removed blanket `_fi.pdf` exclude (it blocked valid `bm_einz_h_erg_fi.pdf` finale files)

Canonical download names prefix year when missing: `bm/bm_sb_he_erg.pdf` → `bm2005_sb_he_erg.pdf`.

## Usage

```powershell
# Verify all seasons 2004–2009
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --probe --first-year 2004 --last-year 2009 --dry-run

# Download SBM 2016 (season folder 2015-16)
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season 2015-16 --category suedbayerische-herren
```

Probe output now includes `index_url` and `index_candidates` so you can see which URL variant was used per season.

**Note:** 2006-07 has fewer files on the index page (no Bayerische Einzel PDFs linked there that year). That’s a source gap on the homepage, not a URL resolution issue. Parser support for pre-2012 PDF layouts is still a separate step after download.

_**Agent (default)**_

There’s no single “download 2004–2018” flag yet — `--probe` covers a year range, but downloads are one season at a time via `--season`.

## 1. Preview first (recommended)

Bowling season `2004-05` holds BM **2005** PDFs; `2017-18` holds **2018** PDFs. For tournament years **2005–2018**, use:

```powershell
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --probe --first-year 2004 --last-year 2017 --dry-run
```

That prints what would be downloaded per season without fetching files.

## 2. Download all categories, all seasons

From the repo root, loop seasons in PowerShell:

```powershell
for ($y = 2004; $y -le 2017; $y++) {
  $yy = "{0:D2}" -f (($y + 1) % 100)
  uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season "$y-$yy"
}
```

That runs 14 seasons (`2004-05` … `2017-18`), all 10 tournament categories each time.

Files go to:

`C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input\`

(alternate: whatever `BOWLYZER_WORK_DATA_DIR` points at). Mirrors also land under `legacy_scrape\saison{YYYY-YY}\meisterschaften\`. Log: `legacy_scrape\tournament_scrape_log.jsonl`.

## 3. Useful options

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--dry-run` | Discover only, no downloads (per season) |
| `--category suedbayerische-herren` | Repeatable; limit to one category |
| `--interval 2.5` | Seconds between PDF downloads (default 2.5) |
| `--output-dir C:\path\to\input` | Override output folder |

Example — only Südbayerische Herren:

```powershell
for ($y = 2004; $y -le 2017; $y++) {
  $yy = "{0:D2}" -f (($y + 1) % 100)
  uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --season "$y-$yy" --category suedbayerische-herren
}
```

## 4. After download → import

```powershell
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py
```

(or `--id sbm-2016-herren` for a single configured job).

**Note:** Expect on the order of ~15 seasons × ~10–20 PDFs each, with 2.5 s between files — roughly 30–60+ minutes total. Already-downloaded files are skipped if they’re ≥ 4 KB on disk.

If you want, I can add `--first-year` / `--last-year` to the download path (same as `--probe`) so you don’t need the loop.

```powershell
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --first-year 2004 --last-year 2017
```

## Dry-run first

```powershell
uv run python scripts/scrape_legacy_tournaments.py --first-year 2004 --last-year 2017 --dry-run
```

## Options

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--category suedbayerische-herren` | Limit to one category (repeatable) |
| `--interval 2.5` | Pause between PDF downloads |
| `--season-interval 5` | Pause between seasons (defaults to `--interval`) |
| `--output-dir C:\path\to\input` | Override output directory |

Output goes to `C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input\` with a per-season summary JSON at the end (`seasons_attempted`, `downloaded`, `skipped_existing`, `failed`, per-season `seasons[]`).

**Modes (mutually exclusive):**
- `--season 2016-17` — single season
- `--probe --first-year … --last-year …` — discover only
- `--first-year … --last-year …` — download range (both years required)

Already-downloaded files are skipped. Progress is logged to `legacy_scrape\tournament_scrape_log.jsonl`.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The import system relies on explicit jobs in tournament_imports.json, each specifying a PDF path and an import ID.

Three approaches are being considered to support import_tournaments.py. One discovers PDFs dynamically by filename pattern. Another extends the configuration with tournament code tags. A third adds a resolver module that maps tournament codes and years to synthetic import entries.

Existing config IDs are inconsistent and contain typos. A new module under `tournament_import/` will map tournament codes and years to expected PDF basenames, reusing scrape patterns or simple globs.

The CLI will accept `--tournament`, `--first-year`, and `--last-year` flags. It resolves these to PDF paths and either auto-generates import entries or runs adapters directly. Calendar year mapping will keep the first-year as season start year for BM seasons.

The import year range will follow the same convention as scraping. A first-year value of 2016 will target the 2017 tournament year, since seasons run from 2016-17 onward.

The calendar year equals the season start year plus one. SBM 2016 corresponds to season 2015-16. To target a calendar year, the user must supply the preceding season start year.

The help text will document the season-start-year convention. Legacy filename patterns from `legacy_tournament_scrape.json` will locate matching PDFs in `tournaments/input/`. A new module, `dynamic_legacy_pdf.py`, will generate calendar years from the season range.

A `find_pdf_for_tournament` helper will scan the input directory for PDFs matching a code and calendar year. A `build_dynamic_entry` helper will synthesize import entries with synthetic IDs like `legacy-sbm-2017`.

The import service will gain a `run_tournaments` method. It will iterate over the requested year range and codes, locate each PDF, and run the adapter with a dynamic entry if found. Missing files will trigger warnings or be skipped.

The CLI will accept `--tournament`, `--first-year`, and `--last-year` flags. It remains to decide whether these should be mutually exclusive or combinable with `--id`.

The CLI will resolve PDFs dynamically when `--tournament` and year flags are used together, while `--id` keeps the existing behavior. Tests will use temporary directories with fixture PDFs. The discovery logic will scan the input directory for PDFs and match them against scrape category patterns to identify the calendar year.

The implementation will use `calendar_years_for_season_range` to compute calendar years from the season range. A `find_legacy_pdf_imports` function will scan the input directory for PDFs matching each tournament code and calendar year. When multiple files match, the resolver will prefer `_akt_` variants or `_erg.pdf` endings. Missing files will trigger warnings and be skipped.

Dynamic ImportEntry objects will use IDs like `legacy-{code}-{year}`. They will target postprocessed CSV outputs and carry `merge_target="manual"` and `enabled=True`. Skip line patterns may be added per code or applied universally to all legacy PDFs.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

`import_tournaments.py` now supports the same tournament shorthand and season year range as the scraper.

### New CLI flags

- `--tournament` — `sbm`, `nbm`, `bm`, `bm_f` (repeatable or comma-separated)
- `--first-year` / `--last-year` — season **start** years (same convention as the scraper)
- `--input-dir` — override PDF directory (default: `work_dir/tournaments/input`)

Use either `--id` (config entries) **or** `--tournament` + year range — not both.

### Example

```powershell
# Dry-run: resolve PDFs and parse without writing
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --first-year 2016 --last-year 2018 --tournament sbm,nbm,bm,bm_f --dry-run

# Full import (CSV merge + parquet + player hybrid)
uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --first-year 2016 --last-year 2018 --tournament sbm,nbm,bm,bm_f
```

### How it works

1. `database/tournament_import/legacy_pdf_targets.py` maps codes → scrape category patterns, finds matching PDFs per calendar year (`season_start + 1`), and prefers `_akt_` / `_erg.pdf` variants.
2. Each match becomes a dynamic `ImportEntry` (`legacy_pdf_erg_2016` adapter) with per-file CSV output like `tournament_legacy_pdf_sbm_2017_postprocessed.csv`.
3. Missing PDFs are listed but do not stop the run.

Remember: `--first-year 2016` targets **2017** PDFs (`bm2017_*`). For calendar-year 2016 SBM (`bm2016_sb_he_erg.pdf`), use `--first-year 2015`.

Modern imports already use "Bayerische Meisterschaft - Frauen Einzel" and "Bayerische Meisterschaft - Männer Einzel". Legacy 2016 men entries use "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel {year}". The proposed fix is "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel Damen {year}" to match BSKV conventions.

The best approach is to define explicit event name templates per tournament code in `legacy_pdf_targets.py`. This would assign distinct names to each legacy source, such as "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel Damen {year}" for bm_f, instead of relying on generic PDF titles that fail to distinguish men's and women's competitions.

Static config entries in `tournament_imports.json` can keep their current overrides. The sbm-2018-frauen entry also needs an explicit event name because it uses the bm_f PDF. A filename-based fallback could infer gender from suffixes like `_da_` or `einz_he`, but the cleanest solution remains adding explicit templates in `legacy_pdf_targets.py`.

A new helper will normalize BM event names by combining the PDF title with the source filename. Gender will be inferred from filename suffixes like `einz_he` for men and `einz_da` for women. This covers both dynamic imports and static config entries without requiring manual overrides.

The helper checks the source filename for gender markers. Suffixes like `einz_he` or `_he_` indicate men's entries, while `einz_da`, `_da_`, or `einzel_d` indicate women's entries. If the PDF title already contains "Damen" or "Frauen", the original title is preserved unchanged.

The helper returns the original title unchanged when the PDF title already contains "Damen" or "Frauen". The 2017 men's PDF title is simply "Bayerische Meisterschaft 2017" without "Einzel", so the helper leaves it untouched.

The disambiguation helper will be named `_disambiguate_event_name` and placed in `legacy_pdf_erg_2016.py`. SBM and NBM titles already carry regional prefixes and "Einzel", so they cannot collide. Only BM herren and bm_f share the same generic PDF title. ### Fix

1. **Filename-based disambiguation** in the PDF parser — tokens like `einz_he` vs `einz_da` / `einz_f` in the PDF filename now produce distinct names:
   - Herren: `Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2017`
   - Damen: `Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel Damen 2017`

2. **Explicit event names** for `--tournament bm` / `bm_f` dynamic imports via `import_entry_for_target`.

Dry-run now shows the split correctly:

```
[legacy-bm-2017] ... events=['Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2017']
[legacy-bm_f-2017] ... events=['Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel Damen 2017']
```

### Re-import

Your manual CSV still has the old ambiguous names from the broken run. Re-run the import, but first remove the stale colliding events (otherwise you'll keep duplicate/wrong rows under the old names):

```powershell
uv run python -c "
from database.tournament_import.io import MANUAL_TOURNAMENT_CSV, strip_event_from_csv
for name in [
    'Bayerische Meisterschaft 2017',
    'Bayerische Meisterschaft 2019',
]:
    n = strip_event_from_csv(MANUAL_TOURNAMENT_CSV, name)
    print(f'removed {n} rows for {name!r}')
"

uv run python scripts/import_tournaments.py --first-year 2016 --last-year 2018 --tournament sbm,nbm,bm,bm_f
```

After that, both competitions should coexist in `tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv` and the parquet.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A test expects `get_aggregate_lifetime_stats` to run for season=all. The current code may short-circuit via `_aggregate_lifetime_from_season_caches` instead. This likely explains why stale cache entries are still being hit.

The test only patches the top-level cache lookup. `_aggregate_lifetime_from_season_caches` calls `league_cache_try_get` separately for each season. Stale entries therefore bypass the mock and still get returned.

The disk merge shortcut should be removed entirely. This aligns with the test expectation and fixes the stale cache issue.

`warm_player_lifetime_career` will switch to live `get_aggregate_lifetime_stats(season="all")` instead of merging per-season disk caches.

`league_cache_invalidate_database` will clear runtime caches too.

Tournament import will invalidate caches after publishing data. A new module will handle this to avoid circular imports.

A new `app/cache/player_data_cache.py` module will define `PLAYER_MERGED_DATABASE` and an `invalidate_player_merged_caches` helper. This helper invalidates the shared pandas adapter cache and clears the revision index for the merged player database.

The invalidation helper will also clear the runtime cache and return counts for both disk and runtime entries removed.

Tournament parquet and league results dataframe caches will be invalidated too.

`effective_data_revision` needs a fix for season=all.

`effective_data_revision` will return `index.global_revision` for season "all".

A `--warm-caches` flag may be added to the import command for immediate cache warming, though invalidation alone is the default. After publishing, the system will print a message telling the user to warm caches or wait for lazy rebuild.

`league_cache_invalidate_database` will also clear runtime caches.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Stale cache is currently active on the running server. Immediate operational steps will be provided to resolve the sync issues.

The in-memory adapter cache auto-reloads when parquet mtime changes. The stale data likely comes from disk JSON cache files that were not invalidated. Restarting the Flask server should force a fresh load.

The revision index on disk is checked against the current parquet mtime. When the data changes, the stored revision no longer matches, so the system discards the stale index and rebuilds it on the next request.

The Gesamt disk merge path was serving incomplete merged caches without verifying completeness; this is now fixed. The season=all cache was built from stale per-season fragments during warm-up, but it should still miss because the global revision changes whenever the full dataframe updates. The remaining stale hits must come from another source.

The running server may be holding an incorrect revision index in memory. The adapter should reload automatically when the tournament parquet mtime changes, but the server might still be using old parquet data. If the import ran without publishing the new parquet file, the revision would not update and the stale cache would persist.

Club 300 is affected by the same stale-cache bug. The Gesamt route merges old per-season caches into a new season-all file without recomputing from live data. This produces incomplete results. The fix resolves itself on the next season-all request once the top-level cache misses. Immediate user actions are being prepared.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

You were hitting a real cache bug, not bad tournament data.

### Root cause

Three things stacked:

1. **Tournament import never invalidated player caches** — `tournaments_postprocessed.parquet` updated, but disk JSON for `get_lifetime_stats?season=all` and `get_club_300` stayed served.
2. **Gesamt built from stale per-season cache files** — on a cache miss, the route merged existing per-season disk caches instead of recomputing from live data. If some seasons were fresh and others stale, Gesamt was incomplete while individual season chips looked fine.
3. **Warm script did the same merge** — `lifetime-career` warm perpetuated the problem.

### Fixes applied

| Change | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `app/cache/player_data_cache.py` | Central invalidation (adapter, revision index, dataframe, disk + runtime caches) |
| `TournamentImportService` | Auto-invalidates player caches after `publish_tournaments_parquet()` |
| `player_routes.get_lifetime_stats` | Gesamt always uses live `get_aggregate_lifetime_stats` |
| `warm_player_cache.py` | Career warm uses live aggregate, not disk merge |
| `league_cache_invalidate_database` | Also clears runtime overlay |
| `effective_data_revision` | `season=all` explicitly uses `global_revision` |

### Fix your environment now (one-time)

The running Flask process still has stale cache entries until you bust them:

```powershell
uv run python -c "from app.cache.player_data_cache import invalidate_player_merged_caches; print(invalidate_player_merged_caches())"
```

Then either restart the Flask dev server, or pre-warm:

```powershell
uv run python scripts/warm_player_cache.py --database db_player_merged_hybrid --phase essential --rebuild
```

After that, Gesamt and Club 300 should reflect all imported tournaments. Future `import_tournaments.py` runs will invalidate automatically (you'll see a message with optional warm command).

---

- when a tournament is selected, show only the table with the top 3 finishers for the selected tournament
- when a season is selected, show one table with the the top 3 finishers of all tournaments of that season
- when both tournament and season is selected, show the regular content
- make it possible, to filter for player w/o the need to select a tournament. present a table with season, touirnament, position and average for all tournaments the player participated in. depending on selection of season or tournament, display less info. when player, tournemen and season are selected, present the known individual results page for the selected event

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Starting with the backend implementation in `tournament_service.py`.

Defining four backend functions in `tournament_service.py`: `get_tournament_events`, `get_tournament_podiums`, `get_all_tournament_players`, and `get_player_tournament_results`. Also drafting a helper to extract the top three finishers from leaderboard tables.

Refining the podium extraction approach. The helper will use TableData field names to parse leaderboard columns directly. A new `_podium_for_event` method will fetch the tournament dataframe, build the KO bracket payload, retrieve the leaderboard table, integrate any KO placements, and return the top N finishers. Also beginning a `_leaderboard_top_n` helper to handle the extraction.

The `_leaderboard_top_n` helper will scan leaderboard columns to locate rank, player, club, and average fields. It will take the first N rows assuming the table is already sorted. KO placements such as "3/3" are handled by the integrated leaderboard. A new `get_player_tournament_history` method will collect player results across events without loading full section pages.

Switching to a faster approach for `get_player_tournament_history`. Instead of checking every event individually, the method will filter the full tournament dataframe by player name and extract unique season-event combinations. It will then compute lightweight summaries for those matches rather than loading full section pages.

The `get_player_tournament_history` implementation will group the filtered dataframe by season and event. It will iterate over each combination, call `get_player_progress_series` to compute progress, KO placement, final position, and average, and return a sorted list of results. This may be slower for large datasets, but it is acceptable for a UI context.

Adding a `get_all_players` helper to return sorted unique names from the tournament dataframe. Planning new API routes with caching. Restructuring the frontend to add new components and rework `TournamentStats`. The view mode logic will show regular content only when both season and tournament are selected, while player-only filtering will display a separate overview table.

Clarifying the frontend view logic. Player-only filtering will show a participation table with season, tournament, position, and average columns. When a season is also selected, the season column will be hidden. The regular individual results page will appear only when a player, season, and tournament are all selected simultaneously.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Helper methods will be added to tournament_service.py.

A `_list_tournament_events` helper is being added to `tournament_service.py`. It builds a list of unique season-event pairs from the tournament DataFrame.

The `_list_tournament_events` helper now sorts results by season descending and tournament name. A `_flatten_table_fields` helper is added to extract field names from nested table columns. A `_leaderboard_top_finishers` method is also being started.

The `_leaderboard_top_finishers` method is being implemented. It accepts season, tournament, an optional DataFrame, and a top_n parameter. It fetches the tournament DataFrame if none is provided. It builds a KO bracket payload and retrieves the leaderboard table. It extracts placements and the KO finale round number.

The method integrates KO bracket data into the total leaderboard when available. It flattens the leaderboard table columns and defines an index helper to locate the rank, player, and club fields.

The method locates the average score column among total_avg, avg_scratch, and avg_net. It iterates over leaderboard rows, parses the rank value to extract the numeric position, and filters out any entries beyond the requested top_n.

The top 3 finishers will be taken from the first three rows of the sorted leaderboard table. This avoids misreading KO bracket ranks such as 3/3 or 5/5.

A `get_player_tournament_results` method is being added to `tournament_service.py`. It normalizes the player name and fetches the tournament DataFrame filtered by season and tournament. It returns an empty list if the DataFrame is empty or lacks a player name column. The implementation is still incomplete.

The `get_player_tournament_results` method is being completed. It filters the DataFrame for the specified player, extracts unique season-event pairs, and begins iterating over those pairs to build the result list.

Inside the `get_player_tournament_results` loop, the method fetches the player's progress series and builds a KO bracket payload. It extracts the player's KO placement and replaces the last entry in the position series with that value. It then filters the average series to numeric values, rounds the last value to one decimal place, and stores it as the tournament average.

The method converts the final position to an integer. It looks up the player's club in the filtered DataFrame and appends a dictionary containing season, tournament, and position to the results list.

The `get_player_tournament_results` method now returns the sorted results list. A `get_tournament_player_catalog` method is being added to retrieve all players from the tournament DataFrame, optionally filtered by season or tournament. The existing `get_players` route requirement may be relaxed to allow catalog access without both parameters. A podiums endpoint is also being planned.

The `get_tournament_podiums` method is being implemented. It lists tournament events and gathers the top finishers for each one. It returns a dictionary containing the top_n limit and a list of podium entries. Each entry maps a season and tournament to its finishers. The finisher data structure is being defined.

Frontend component planning is underway. `TournamentPodiumTable.tsx` will render podiums grouped by tournament or season depending on the current view mode. `TournamentPlayerHistoryTable.tsx` will display a player's tournament participation history. `TournamentStats.tsx` needs updated view mode logic. The filter bar will be extended to support player search without requiring a tournament selection.

The `useTournamentNames` hook will be enabled when no season is selected. A new global `useTournamentPlayers` hook is being introduced.

Clicking a player in the podium table will set the player filter parameter. Clicking a tournament or season row will navigate to the detail view. Podium entries will include links to filter directly to that event.

The implementation plan covers adding service methods and routes, cache keys, frontend hooks, table components, and updates to `TournamentStats` and `TournamentFilterBar`, plus tests for podium extraction.</details></think>
