_**Agent (default)**_

The tournament landing page now supports overview modes and optional filters without auto-selecting a season/tournament.

### View modes

| Filters | Content |
|---------|---------|
| None | Podium table — top 3 for **every** tournament (season + tournament columns) |
| Season only | Podium table — top 3 for all tournaments in that season |
| Tournament only | Podium table — top 3 for that tournament across seasons |
| Season + tournament | **Existing detail view** (leaderboard, cards, KO, etc.) |
| Player only | Participation table: season, tournament, position, average |
| Player + season | Same table, season column hidden |
| Player + tournament | Same table, tournament column hidden |
| Player + season + tournament | **Existing player detail view** |

### Backend (new endpoints)

- `GET /tournament/get_tournament_podiums?season=&tournament=&n=3`
- `GET /tournament/get_player_tournament_results?player=&season=&tournament=`
- `GET /tournament/get_available_players` — works without season/tournament (global player catalog for search)

Podium ranks use the same final leaderboard logic as the detail page (including KO integration).

### Frontend

- Removed auto-backfill of latest season / first tournament — `/turnier` opens on the overview
- Player search works without selecting a tournament first
- Click **player** in podium → sets player filter (overview)
- Click **season/tournament** in podium → jumps to event detail
- Click a row in the player overview → opens full player results for that event

Restart the Flask dev server so the new routes are picked up, then open `/turnier` to try the overview.

---

_**User**_

clarification:
http://127.0.0.1:5000/turnier 
should deliver one table per tournament, one row for each season. 3 cols "Position 1-3" that holds the respecive players name. the names serve as deep link to the player event page. 
each of the tables should live inside a foldable container and feature the tournament name as headline
when one season is selected, the same table should be extended for one col holding the tournament name (abbreviation, with full name in the tooltip). cell with tournament name is deep link to event, player names are deep links to player event page.

---

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The API returns 19 podiums with finishers. The empty containers likely stem from frontend rendering.

Collapsible sections are hidden by default. DataTable mounts inside zero-size containers. Tabulator cannot render rows. The `isArrayFormat` check may also fail for object-format data.

DataTable mounts while the section is collapsed. Tabulator renders inside a zero-height hidden div. Opening the section does not trigger a redraw because the effect only runs when data changes. Lazy mounting the table only when the section is open would fix this.

Other fixes include calling `tabulator.redraw()` when the section opens, or replacing the `hidden` attribute with CSS visibility or height animations. The preferred solution is to lift the open state to the parent and only render the DataTable when the section is actually open. The single-season table should work correctly since it is not collapsible.

The user might be seeing empty containers even after expanding the section. If so, the cause is different. Otherwise, the `hidden` attribute forces zero dimensions during initialization. CollapsibleSection does not easily expose its open state, so conditionally rendering the DataTable only when the section is open remains the cleanest fix.

The chosen fix is to conditionally render children only when the section is open. This ensures the DataTable mounts fresh with correct dimensions rather than initializing inside a zero-size hidden container.</details></think>

The API was returning data (19 tournaments with finishers). The problem was **Tabulator initializing inside collapsed foldables** — panels use `hidden`, so the table got zero height and stayed blank even after expanding.

### Fixes
1. **`lazyMount` on `CollapsibleSection`** — the DataTable only mounts when a section is open, so Tabulator gets a real layout.
2. **Array row format** for podium tables (same as other backend tables).
3. **First tournament section open by default** so `/turnier` shows data immediately without expanding everything.

Hard-refresh `/turnier` (or rebuild the frontend if you serve a production bundle). You should see the first podium table right away; others populate when you expand them.

---

_**User**_

there is some overly specific naming that causes fragmentation of the displayed results. 
e.g. "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2018" and seasons 2017/18.
it should be "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel" and the season is separate. this allows for better grouping

---

Tournament names are now normalized for grouping and display, while the full DB event name is still used for links and detail views.

### What changed

**Backend** (`app/utils/tournament_utils.py`):
- Added `normalize_tournament_group_name()` — strips trailing years (`… 2018`) and maps GF/legacy variants to one label (e.g. `"Bayerische Meisterschaft - Männer Einzel"` → `"Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel"`, `"Nordbayerische Meisterschaft"` → `"Nordbayrische Meisterschaft Einzel"`).

**Filtering** (`tournament_service.py`):
- Tournament filters accept either the exact DB name or the normalized group name.
- `get_available_tournaments` returns deduplicated group names.
- Podium and player-result APIs include `tournament_group`.

**Frontend** (`tournamentOverviewTables.ts`):
- Foldable sections group by `tournament_group`.
- Season view shows abbreviations of the group name; tooltip still shows the full event name (with year).
- Player participation table shows the group name.

### Result

Instead of separate foldables for `"Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2016"`, `"… 2017"`, `"… 2018"`, you get one **"Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel"** section with rows per season (`15/16`, `16/17`, `17/18`, …). GF and legacy naming for the same event type are grouped together where aliases apply.

Stored CSV/parquet names are unchanged; deep links still use the exact `tournament` query param from the row data.

_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is asking an unrelated architectural question about replacing the backend tech stack with Rust for a data-heavy application.

Rust is a solid fit for this data-heavy backend. The existing Flask and Python stack handles heavy CSV and parquet workloads, so Rust can deliver the same performance with stronger type safety and memory control. A proper database and repository layer would pair well with Rust's ownership model.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Yes — Rust is a solid choice for a data-heavy REST API backend, and your planned rewrite (proper DB, repositories, stricter boundaries) is exactly the kind of project where Rust pays off. It is feasible; the real question is how much of the *data pipeline* you move vs keep.

## Why Rust fits this use case

Your app is a good match for Rust’s strengths:

- **Read-heavy APIs** — league standings, player aggregates, tournament podiums, cached responses. Lots of predictable query → serialize → JSON.
- **Performance under load** — lower latency and memory than a Flask monolith, especially if you drop per-request pandas work.
- **Concurrency** — async I/O (Postgres, Redis, disk cache) without GIL limits; parallel aggregation where it helps.
- **Long-lived correctness** — types + explicit error handling suit a domain with seasons, rounds, KO brackets, handicaps, etc.

For REST, the ecosystem is mature:

| Layer | Common choices |
|--------|----------------|
| HTTP framework | **Axum** (most popular now), Actix Web |
| Async runtime | **Tokio** |
| DB | **sqlx** or **Diesel** with Postgres |
| Serialization | **serde** + JSON |
| Migrations | sqlx migrate, refinery |
| Caching | Redis (`fred`, `redis` crate) or in-process |

You can absolutely build a fast, clean REST API in Rust.

## Where Rust is harder than Python (for *your* project)

The friction is usually not the API layer — it’s the **analytics / ETL side**:

- Today you have pandas, CSV/parquet workflows, import scripts, and a lot of bowling-specific logic in Python.
- Rust has **Polars**, **Arrow**, **datafusion**, but the ergonomics for one-off imports, Excel/PDF parsing, and iterative data fixes are still behind Python.
- Re-implementing every import adapter and validation rule in Rust is a large, slow part of the rewrite.

So the pragmatic split many teams use:

```text
Rust API service          Python (or Rust batch jobs)
     │                              │
     ├─ REST / auth / caching       ├─ imports (XLSX, PDF, scrape)
     ├─ read models / aggregates    ├─ publish to DB / parquet
     └─ Postgres queries            └─ one-off data repairs
```

That gives you Rust where you want speed and structure, without rewriting every scraper on day one.

## Is Rust “worth it” for you?

**Strong yes** if your goals are:

- Learning Rust on a real project
- Stable API contracts for the React frontend
- Postgres as source of truth with explicit repositories
- Predictable performance on VPS/small hardware
- Fewer runtime surprises in production

**Pause and simplify** if you mainly want:

- Faster delivery of features
- Heavy ad-hoc data exploration and imports
- Minimal ops complexity with a tiny team

For a follow-up rewrite with clear architecture, Rust is a *good* choice — not mandatory. **Go** would also work well (simpler, fast enough). **Staying on Python** with FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Postgres is totally valid if the bottleneck is data modeling, not language speed.

## A realistic Rust architecture for Bowl-A-Lyzer

Something like:

```text
React  →  Rust API (Axum)
              │
              ├─ handlers (thin)
              ├─ services (domain rules: KO, handicap, standings)
              ├─ repositories (sqlx → Postgres)
              └─ read models / materialized views for heavy pages

Import pipeline (Python or Rust CLI) → Postgres (+ optional parquet archive)
```

Key design choices that matter more than Rust vs Python:

1. **Precompute aggregates** — don’t rebuild leaderboards from raw game rows on every request (you’re already moving this way with caches).
2. **Stable API shapes** — keep the React strangler-fig contract; version endpoints if needed.
3. **Import vs serve separation** — imports are batch jobs; API is read-optimized.
4. **Materialized views or summary tables** — player career stats, season podiums, club matrices.

Rust shines once serving is “query precomputed tables + a bit of logic,” not “load a dataframe and pivot.”

## Learning curve (honest)

- **First 2–4 weeks**: Axum + sqlx + serde feels productive.
- **1–3 months**: error handling, lifetimes, async patterns click.
- **3–6 months**: you’ll want a clear module layout (your DDD-ish plan helps).

Start with one vertical slice: e.g. `GET /tournament/podiums` backed by Postgres, mirroring current JSON. That validates the stack without a big-bang rewrite.

## Bottom line

**Yes — Rust is a good fit for a data-heavy REST backend** when you commit to a real database, repositories, and precomputed read models. It’s an especially good “learn Rust properly” project because the domain is bounded and the frontend already wants JSON APIs.

I’d use Rust for the **API + domain + persistence layer**, and either keep Python for **imports/ETL** initially or migrate those incrementally. That avoids turning the rewrite into “rebuild pandas in Rust.”

If you want, I can sketch a concrete target layout (crates, modules, which current Flask endpoints map to which Postgres tables) as a migration blueprint without touching code.

It covers:

- **Prerequisite** — start only after legacy data is reliably published
- **Goals / non-goals** — Postgres, repositories, fast REST; not a big-bang import rewrite
- **Rust fit** — API + domain + DB yes; ETL/imports stay Python initially
- **Target architecture** — Axum, sqlx, Postgres, read models / materialized views
- **Strangler-fig migration** — vertical slices, `/api/v2` routing, golden JSON parity tests
- **Phased roadmap** — data → schema → Rust slice → core reads → import-to-DB → cutover
- **Risks, open questions, and a concrete first spike** when you're ready

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The legacy CSV contains a Cut Line column, but it is empty.

Three approaches are being considered to populate the missing cut lines: extending the tournament config with per-round cut values, updating the stage definitions JSON for legacy tournaments, or post-processing the CSVs during import. The user wants the CSV results scanned to determine the correct cuts.

The plan is to extend the stage definitions JSON for legacy tournaments and wire tournament_service to consume it when CSV Cut Lines are missing. The GF export mechanism is being checked to determine whether the existing stage definitions file can be reused or if tournament_ko_config needs expansion instead.

The stage definitions JSON is keyed by tournament type and year. Legacy events carry season identifiers such as 17/18. A script will scan the parquet and CSV files for three-round tournaments. Cuts will be derived from the player count advancing to the next round. These values will be added to the existing stage definitions or a new legacy file. The tournament service will then resolve missing Cut Lines from this config.</details></think>

    Path('database/data/tournaments_postprocessed.parquet'),
    Path('database/data/tournament_manual_postprocessed.csv'),
]
dfs = []
for p in paths:
    if p.suffix == '.parquet' and p.is_file():
        dfs.append(pd.read_parquet(p))
    elif p.suffix == '.csv' and p.is_file():
        dfs.append(pd.read_csv(p, sep=';', low_memory=False))
if not dfs:
    print('no data')
    raise SystemExit
df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
df = df[df['Event Type'].astype(str).str.lower().eq('tournament')]
# normalize cols
for c in ['Season','Event Name','Round Number','Round Name','Player','Player ID','Game Number','Date','Location']:
    if c not in df.columns:
        print('missing', c)

events = df.groupby(['Season','Event Name']).agg(
    rounds=('Round Number', lambda s: sorted(set(int(x) for x in pd.to_numeric(s, errors='coerce').dropna()))),
    round_names=('Round Name', lambda s: sorted(set(str(x).strip() for x in s.dropna().unique()))),
).reset_index()

three_tier = []
for _, row in events.iterrows():
    names = [n.lower() for n in row['round_names']]
    if any('vorlauf' in n for n in names) and any('zwischen' in n for n in names) and any('finale' in n for n in names):
        three_tier.append(row)

print(f'total tournament events: {len(events)}')
print(f'3-tier events: {len(three_tier)}')
print()

for _, row in sorted(three_tier, key=lambda r: (r['Season'], r['Event Name'])):
    season, ev = row['Season'], row['Event Name']
    sub = df[(df['Season']==season)&(df['Event Name']==ev)]
    cuts = {}
    games_per_round = {}
    for rn in row['rounds']:
        rsub = sub[pd.to_numeric(sub['Round Number'], errors='coerce').eq(rn)]
        players = rsub['Player'].astype(str).str.strip().nunique()
        rn_name = rsub['Round Name'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().mode()
        rn_name = rn_name.iloc[0] if len(rn_name) else f'Round {rn}'
        max_game = pd.to_numeric(rsub['Game Number'], errors='coerce').max()
        games = int(max_game)+1 if pd.notna(max_game) else 0
        games_per_round[int(rn)] = games
        cuts[int(rn)] = (rn_name, players)
    # infer cut = players in next round
    stage_cuts = []
    rounds = row['rounds']
    for i, rn in enumerate(rounds):
        name, players = cuts[rn]
        if i+1 < len(rounds):
            next_players = cuts[rounds[i+1]][1]
            stage_cuts.append((rn, name, next_players, games_per_round[rn]))
        else:
            stage_cuts.append((rn, name, None, games_per_round[rn]))
    date = sub['Date'].dropna().astype(str).mode()
    date = date.iloc[0] if len(date) else ''
    loc = sub['Location'].dropna().astype(str).mode()
    loc = loc.iloc[0] if len(loc) else ''
    print(f'{season} | {ev}')
    for rn, name, cut, games in stage_cuts:
        print(f'  r{rn} {name}: {games} games, cut->{cut}')
    print()

```bash
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
```
from glob import glob
import json

files = glob('database/data/tournament_*postprocessed.csv')
df = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f, sep=';', low_memory=False) for f in files], ignore_index=True)
df = df[df['Event Type'].astype(str).str.lower().eq('tournament')]

def analyze(season, ev):
    sub = df[(df['Season'].astype(str).str.strip()==season)&(df['Event Name'].astype(str).str.strip()==ev)]
    rounds = sorted(int(x) for x in pd.to_numeric(sub['Round Number'], errors='coerce').dropna().unique())
    stages = []
    game_start = 1
    for rn in rounds:
        rsub = sub[pd.to_numeric(sub['Round Number'], errors='coerce').eq(rn)]
        name = rsub['Round Name'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().mode().iloc[0]
        max_game = int(pd.to_numeric(rsub['Game Number'], errors='coerce').max())
        games = max_game + 1
        players = rsub['Player'].astype(str).str.strip().nunique()
        date = rsub['Date'].dropna().astype(str).mode()
        date = date.iloc[0] if len(date) else ''
        loc = rsub['Location'].dropna().astype(str).mode()
        loc = loc.iloc[0] if len(loc) else ''
        stages.append({'id': rn, 'name': name, 'players': players, 'games': games, 'game_start': game_start, 'game_end': game_start+games-1, 'date': date, 'location': loc})
        game_start += games
    cuts = []
    for i, st in enumerate(stages):
        cut = stages[i+1]['players'] if i+1 < len(stages) else None
        cuts.append(cut)
    return stages, cuts

targets = []
for (season, ev), _ in df.groupby(['Season','Event Name']):
    sub = df[(df['Season']==season)&(df['Event Name']==ev)]
    names = ' '.join(sub['Round Name'].dropna().astype(str).str.lower().unique())
    if 'vorlauf' in names and 'zwischen' in names and ('finale' in names or 'finalrunde' in names or 'ko-finale' in names):
        targets.append((str(season).strip(), str(ev).strip()))

out = {}
for season, ev in sorted(targets):
    stages, cuts = analyze(season, ev)
    key = f'{season}||{ev}'
    out[key] = {
        'season': season,
        'event_name': ev,
        'default_location': stages[0]['location'] if stages else '',
        'stages': []
    }
    for st, cut in zip(stages, cuts):
        out[key]['stages'].append({
            'round_number': st['id'],
            'name': st['name'],
            'cut': str(cut) if cut is not None else 'n/a',
            'cut_basis': 'overall_total',
            'evaluation': 'Scratch Total',
            'date': st['date'],
            'location': st['location'],
            'game_start': st['game_start'],
            'game_end': st['game_end'],
            'players': st['players'],
        })
    print(key)
    for st, cut in zip(stages, cuts):
        print(f'  r{st[\"id\"]} {st[\"name\"]}: {st[\"players\"]} players, {st[\"games\"]} games, cut={cut}')
    print()

# also check parquet-only
p = Path('database/data/tournaments_postprocessed.parquet')
if p.is_file():
    pdf = pd.read_parquet(p)
    pdf = pdf[pdf['Event Type'].astype(str).str.lower().eq('tournament')]
    print('parquet events', pdf.groupby(['Season','Event Name']).ngroups)

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Round 3 currently shows "n/a" for its cutline. The official GF cut 12 belongs to the end of Round 2 (Zwischenlauf), not Round 3 (Finale).

The test expectation needs correction: round 3 should be None. The field progress list [79, 40, 6] incorrectly appends cut 6 for round 3. This likely stems from a fallback value such as `ko_qualifying_cut_rank` or the gesamt cut rank 6. For legacy SBM 2018, the tournament config probably lacks a round 3 entry, and the span fallback does not apply.

The loop appends `last_cut_pos` whenever `in_cut_span` is true and `cut_pos_round` is None. This explains why round 3 still receives cut position 6.

The root cause is now clear: `in_cut_span` evaluates to True because `cfg_span` is None, even though round 3 has no configured cut. This causes the loop to fall back to `last_cut_pos` (6) instead of leaving the round empty. The fix is to derive `in_cut_span` from the round's actual `stage_cut`, ensuring it is only True when a cut exists for that specific round.</details></think>

Legacy regional tournaments had empty `Cut Line` columns — only GF exports (via `gf_tournament_stage_definitions.json`) populated them. That’s now fixed.

### What was done

**1. Generated `database/data/tournament_stage_definitions.json`** (18 events)  
Scanned all tournament CSVs + parquet for 3-tier events (Vorlauf → Zwischenlauf → Finale/Finalrunde). Cuts are inferred from how many players appear in the next round, except:
- **25/26 Südbayerische Meisterschaft** → official 80 / 40 / 12 (from GF config)
- **25/26 Nordbayerische Meisterschaft** → official 72 / 36 / 12

**2. Runtime wiring** (`app/utils/tournament_stage_config.py` + `tournament_service.py`)
- `_resolved_cut_position_for_round` falls back to stage config when CSV has no cut
- Field-progress charts use **per-round** cut ranks (79/40 for SBM 2018, not a flat “top 6”)
- `get_tournament_format` exposes `qualifying_stages` for the format popup

**3. Import postprocess** (`database/tournament_import/postprocess.py`)  
Future imports fill `Cut Line` / `Cut Basis` from the same config (overall-total ranking, matching GF export).

**4. Regenerator** — after new tournaments are published:
```bash
uv run python scripts/generate_tournament_stage_definitions.py
```

### Result

_**Agent (default)**_

Two issues caused the broken charts:

1. **Group name vs config key** — URLs like `tournament=Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel` use the normalized group label, but stage definitions are keyed as `17/18||Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel 2018`. Lookups failed and the code fell back to a default **top 6** cut (`[6, 6, 6]`), with empty/wrong cut-line series.

2. **Stale disk cache** — old `field-progress-v4` entries could still serve pre-fix payloads.

### Fixes

- **`_config_event_name()`** — resolves the canonical event name from the loaded dataframe (single event in scope) or by matching the group name within the season.
- **Stage/cut lookups** — field progress, cut resolution, and format info all use that resolved name.
- **Cache bump** — `get_tournament_field_progress` → `field-progress-v5` so stale entries are ignored.

After restarting Flask (or waiting for a cache miss), your URL should return cuts `[40, 20]` and working leader/dynamic cut-line charts. GF events like Südbayerische Meisterschaft 25/26 should show `[80, 40, 12]` again.

If charts are still empty, clear the league cache or run `uv run python scripts/warm_league_cache.py` for the tournament database.

---

_**User**_

the cutlines are now visible in the results table and seem plausible. currently, when a stage has no cut line (like most of the old tournaments' final stages) all participants are marked as out of cut and are shown in red. in case a round is not marked with a cutline, assume the cutline to be the number of participants.

The issue on the individual stats page is still not fixed:
http://127.0.0.1:5000/turnier?tournament=S%C3%BCdbayerische+Meisterschaft+Einzel&season=18%2F19&round=3&player=Kloos+Fabian 
the graphs for average and position only show the selected player, but are missing tournament leader and cutlines



---

The GF SBM 25/26 round 3 is labeled "Finale" rather than "KO-Finale" despite having a cut of 12 in the stage configuration.

The cut of 12 for round 3 Finale is the threshold for advancing from the zwischenlauf to the finale. It does not apply as a cut within the finale itself.

The cut values in the GF stage definitions likely describe advancement thresholds between stages. Round 1 Vorlauf uses cut 80, round 2 Zwischenlauf uses cut 40, and round 3 Finale uses cut 12. This implies the finale cluster may have an incorrect cut line in the GF configuration. The test expectation [80, 40, 12] assumes a cut at the end of round 3.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Two separate bugs were fixed:

### 1. Final stage — everyone shown in red
When no cut was configured (e.g. Finalrunde with `cut: n/a`), `_resolved_cut_position_for_round` returned `None`. The table then applied no green/yellow cell styles, and the frontend treated those rows as **outside the cut** (red).

**Fix:** If no cut is defined, use the **number of players in that round** as the effective cut. Everyone ranks inside or on the cut, so no false red rows.

### 2. Player page — missing leader & cut lines
`PlayerSection` expected `field_progress` from `sectionQuery`, but that query is **disabled** on the player detail view (`showPlayerDetail` is true). Leader and cut-line series were always `undefined`.

**Fix:**
- `get_player_section` now includes `field_progress` (same payload as the event overview).
- `TournamentStats` passes `playerSectionQuery.data.field_progress` into `PlayerSection`.
- Cache revision bumped so old player-section responses are dropped.

After a Flask restart, your URL (`Südbayerische Meisterschaft Einzel`, `18/19`, Kloos Fabian) should show:
- **Turnierführung** (purple leader line)
- **Cut-Line** (dynamic or horizontal, depending on toggle)
- Correct cut shading on round 3 (all finalists green/yellow, not red)

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The Python function `_group_alias_lookup` maps long names and aliases to canonical tournament names.

The TypeScript alias map currently lacks the CSV entries present in Python. I will extend `tournamentGroupName.ts` to match `_group_alias_lookup` more closely. Python resolves abbreviations through direct lookup, normalized name lookup, or returning the raw key. Normalization may fail if the exact long name is missing from the CSV.

Backend abbreviation resolution may also fail for grouped names. The alias map contains "Bayerische Meisterschaft Männer Einzel" but the lookup expects "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel", so the entry is missed.

Three approaches are being weighed to fix abbreviation resolution. The first adds canonical group names directly to the backend CSV. The second builds a reverse mapping from abbreviations back to canonical names. The third would iterate over aliases inside `formatCompetitionLabel`, but that seems too heavy.

The simplest fix is a static map from canonical group names to abbreviations. This lets `formatCompetitionLabel` resolve abbreviations even when the normalized key is missing from the alias lookup.

Extending the backend lookup to register normalized canonical names would fix both the API and the frontend. However, the frontend-only approach is preferred because the user specified no backend API changes during the migration.

Concrete mappings for the frontend abbreviation map are now defined. Nordbayerische Meisterschaft becomes NBM M. Nordbayerische Meisterschaft Damen Einzel becomes NBM D. Südbayerische Meisterschaft becomes SBM M. Südbayerische Meisterschaft Damen Einzel becomes SBM D. Bayerische Meisterschaft - Männer Einzel becomes BM M.

The abbreviation map will live in `tournamentGroupName.ts` or `competitionDisplayName.ts`. Static CSV alias entries will be hardcoded there to replicate Python’s `_group_alias_lookup`. `formatCompetitionLabel` will normalize the label and look up the canonical group name.

Doppel tournaments expose another gap. Normalization strips years, but the alias lookup uses the full year-stamped long name. For example, "Bayerische Meisterschaft Männer Doppel 2018" does not match the lookup key "Bayerische Meisterschaft - Männer Doppel". The same mismatch occurs for clubmeisterschaft entries like CM DB 26. These cases likely lack canonical aliases entirely, so the group name remains as-is.

The messy edge cases are being resolved by adding a `buildGroupAliasLookup()` helper that replicates Python’s `_group_alias_lookup` using CSV long names and aliases. The `TOURNAMENT_GROUP_ABBREVIATIONS` map will cover canonical group names produced by `normalizeTournamentGroupName`. Doppel variants and clubmeisterschaft entries will be checked against Börding’s data to decide whether to extend the alias map further.</details></think>

Tournament clustering for **Wettbewerbsübersicht** and **Spielanteil** is implemented.

### What changed

1. **`frontend/src/lib/tournamentGroupName.ts`** (new)  
   Mirrors Python `normalize_tournament_group_name()` — strips trailing years (`… 2016`) and maps GF/legacy name variants to one canonical group (e.g. all Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel years → `Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel`).

2. **`frontend/src/lib/playerCompetitionBreakdown.ts`**  
   Added `clusterTournamentEntries()` (same pattern as `clusterLeagueEntries()`). Tournament rows are merged by group before the bar and pie charts are built. Tooltips list per-year breakdown as `BM M 2016`, `BM M 2018`, etc.

3. **`frontend/src/lib/competitionDisplayName.ts`**  
   Abbreviation lookup now resolves grouped names → `BM M`, `NBM M`, `SBM M`, `BM D`, etc.

4. **Hint text** updated to mention that tournament years are grouped too.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Planning the implementation for data normalization and the tournament validation frontend.

A new `tournament_data_normalization.py` module will handle club name normalization, player ID and name standardization, and registry application. The tournament import service will be updated to run this normalization after row postprocessing.

The `merge_tournament_sources` function will apply normalization before publishing and return statistics. A new `tournament_data_quality.py` module will audit per-season and per-event data quality. It will count missing player IDs and clubs. It will flag normalized club cells and player ID conflicts. It will assign a color-coded status and compile findings.

The existing player ID audit function requires a file path, so it cannot be easily reused on filtered dataframe slices. Instead, lightweight conflict checks will be implemented directly inside `tournament_data_quality.py`. These checks will detect cases where the same player name maps to multiple IDs, or the same ID maps to multiple names, within each event group.

Extending the existing league validation service to include tournament quality metrics on the same page. Tournament rows will be returned alongside league rows, or unified with a kind field. The frontend table will need new columns to display these tournament-specific numbers.

Two separate tables will appear on the same validation page. The existing league table stays unchanged. A new "Turnier-Datenqualität" section will list each tournament event with its own row. This avoids mixing league and tournament columns.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Deciding between extending the league validation API or creating a separate tournament data quality endpoint. Both would be fetched by the frontend hook.

Extending the existing league validation endpoint is cleaner than adding a separate route. The response will include a nested tournament object with source, presence, row count, summary counts, and rows. The frontend hook and backend service will be updated minimally to load this data.

Adding normalization parameters to `merge_tournament_sources` with defaults enabled. The tournament import service will apply `normalize_tournament_dataframe` to postprocessed records and preserve column order. A new `TournamentQualityComparison` dataclass will drive the audit, with CSV output columns for season and event name.

The audit schema now includes normalized group names, player and club counts, missing identifiers, remapped player IDs, registry changes, duplicate name or ID pairs, status flags, and findings. The audit targets normalized published data. A per-event conflict detector is being implemented to count player issues.

The conflict detector normalizes player names and IDs within each tournament group. It tallies same-name duplicates that carry different IDs. A second pass will flag same-ID duplicates that carry different names.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Tournament data quality normalization and validation are wired through the pipeline and the diagnose UI.

### Normalization (like league merge)

**`data_access/tournament_data_normalization.py`** applies the same rules as league merge:
- **Club** → `team_name_normalization.json` (via `normalize_team_name`)
- **Player ID** → `player_id_name_normalization.json` (ID-only remaps)
- **Player name** → `players_registry`

Applied in:
- **`database/tournament_import/service.py`** — after Excel/PDF postprocess, before CSV write
- **`scripts/publish_tournament_parquet.py`** — on each input file before publishing `tournaments_postprocessed.parquet`

### Per-tournament audit

**`data_access/tournament_data_quality.py`** — one row per `season × event_name` with:
- missing player IDs / clubs
- same-name→different-ID and same-ID→different-name conflicts
- status: **green** / **yellow** / **red**

**`scripts/audit_tournament_data_quality.py`** writes `{work}/tournament_data_quality.csv`  
Also runs automatically in **`build_published_dataset.py`** after tournament merge (skip with `--skip-tournament-data-quality-audit`).

### Diagnose UI

**`/diagnose/liga-validierung`** now includes:
- **Turnier-Datenqualität** table — one row per tournament
- KPI chips (green / yellow / red / event count)
- Respects season filter and “Nur nicht grün”

**`/diagnose/datenpipeline`** shows Turnier-Validierung row count.

The API response from `/pipeline/league_standings_validation` includes `tournament_quality` (live from published parquet if no report CSV exists).

### To refresh your local data

```bash
uv run python scripts/build_published_dataset.py --job tournament
# or audit only:
uv run python scripts/audit_tournament_data_quality.py
```

Then reload `http://127.0.0.1:5000/diagnose/liga-validierung?database=db_real_merged`.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The root cause is that `apply_tournament_competition_schema_v2` renames `Event Name` to `Event` and drops the original column.

Audit checks for `Event Name`, but normalization and schema v2 rename it to `Event`. The fix resolves the event column using both aliases in `tournament_data_quality.py`.

Normalization uses the original `Event Name` column before schema v2 renames it, so it likely needs no changes.

Manifest normalization statistics may be missing because `build_published_dataset` does not pass the `merge_tournament_sources` result into the manifest.

The zero-row `player_id_name_audit` is probably caused by the audit path ordering: the audit runs on `tournaments_out` before the tournament merge completes.

Two separate issues — both are addressed.

### Why the audit showed 0 rows

Published tournament data uses schema v2: **`Event Name` is renamed to `Event`** during `apply_tournament_competition_schema_v2()`. The audit only looked for `Event Name`, so it returned nothing even with 19 293 rows.

The audit now resolves **`Event`** or **`Event Name`**. On your parquet I get **19 tournaments** (14 green, 5 yellow, 0 red).

Re-run the publish/audit so the work-dir CSV is regenerated:

```bash
uv run python scripts/audit_tournament_data_quality.py
# or full tournament job:
uv run python scripts/build_published_dataset.py --job tournament
```

### Tiered Validierung UI

| Route | Content |
|--------|---------|
| `/diagnose/validierung` | **Hub** — summary KPIs only (Liga: perfect/corrected/yellow/red/skipped; Turniere: green/yellow/red) |
| `/diagnose/validierung/liga` | Full league validation (unchanged behaviour) |
| `/diagnose/validierung/turniere` | Full tournament table (one row per event) |

- Sidebar: **Validierung** → hub  
- `/diagnose/liga-validierung` redirects to `/diagnose/validierung/liga` (query string preserved)  
- Datenpipeline links point to the hub

Normalization still runs on import/publish; its stats are in the merge summary (`normalization` on the tournaments block). The visible effect is in the per-tournament audit after re-run.

tp = resolve_load_path(tournaments_postprocessed_csv())
lp = resolve_load_path(league_results_merged_csv())

l = pd.read_parquet(lp) if str(lp).endswith('.parquet') else pd.read_csv(lp, sep=';', dtype=str)

tclubs = sorted(t['Club'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().unique()) if 'Club' in t.columns else []
lteams = sorted(l['Team'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().unique()) if 'Team' in l.columns else []

    n = normalize_team_name(name) or name

    m = re.match(r'^(.*?)(?:\s+(\d+))?$', n.strip())

```bash
cd c:\Users\cfell\repositories\bowlyzer_deploy; uv run python -c "
import pandas as pd
from data_access.parquet_sidecar import resolve_load_path
from database.paths import tournaments_postprocessed_csv, league_results_merged_csv
from extract_excel_data import normalize_team_name

tp = resolve_load_path(tournaments_postprocessed_csv())
lp = resolve_load_path(league_results_merged_csv())
t = pd.read_parquet(tp) if str(tp).endswith('.parquet') else pd.read_csv(tp, sep=';', dtype=str)
l = pd.read_parquet(lp) if str(lp).endswith('.parquet') else pd.read_csv(lp, sep=';', dtype=str)

tclubs = sorted(t['Club'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().unique()) if 'Club' in t.columns else []
lteams = sorted(l['Team'].dropna().astype(str).str.strip().unique()) if 'Team' in l.columns else []

# club base from team
def base(name):
    from extract_excel_data import normalize_team_name
    n = normalize_team_name(name) or name
    import re
    m = re.match(r'^(.*?)(?:\s+(\d+))?$', n.strip())
    return (m.group(1) or '').strip() if m else n

lbases = {base(x) for x in lteams}
# tournament clubs that don't match any league club base after normalize_team_name
unmatched = []
for c in tclubs:
    cn = normalize_team_name(c) or c
    if cn in lbases or c in lbases:
        continue
    # try stripping verein prefix patterns
    unmatched.append(c)

print('tournament unique clubs', len(tclubs))
print('league unique team bases', len(lbases))
print('tournament clubs sample', tclubs[:15])
print('unmatched after norm (first 25):')
for x in unmatched[:25]:
    print(' ', repr(x), '->', repr(normalize_team_name(x)))
print('total unmatched', len(unmatched))
"
```

I have enough context to draft a thorough discussion document on building a canonical club name list and validating tournament entries against it.

This mismatch explains why current validation logic does not work.

Runtime club resolution comes from normalized league Team columns. The player registry stores only player IDs and names, with no club field. A dedicated club normalization service exists, but no persisted club mapping file like tournament_mapping.csv. This leaves no centralized canonical club list.

Tournament data contains 98 unique club labels. Most do not match normalized league club bases. Formats vary widely. Examples include GF regional prefixes and bare names. The recommended approach is to derive the canonical list from league results. Distinct club names will be extracted by normalizing team strings and extracting club labels.

Three implementation paths are under consideration.

An audit script could identify club aliases by comparing tournament clusters against normalized league names. Tournament labels would be cleaned by stripping GF prefixes and "e.V." before fuzzy matching.

A dedicated `club_name_normalization.json` could mirror the team mapping format. It would combine league and tournament clusters into canonical names with aliases. GF prefixes would need manual curation.

Alternatively the existing team normalization pipeline could be reused. Tournament clubs would be parsed through `normalize_team_name`, stripped of numbers, and compared directly.

Reusing the existing team normalization pipeline conflates team and club concerns. A GF official Verein list from their API or exports could provide authoritative regional data. A three-phase hybrid approach is also being considered: derive candidates from league data, audit tournament clubs into a conflicts file, then persist the mapping.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Here is what the codebase actually has today, and how I'd approach a canonical club list.

## 1. Do we have a canonical club name list?

**Not as a dedicated, maintained club registry.** What exists is fragmented:

| Source | What it is | Good for tournaments? |
|--------|------------|------------------------|
| [`database/relational_csv/club.csv`](database/relational_csv/club.csv) | ~18 clubs from an old relational build | No — tiny, stale |
| [`database/config/team_name_normalization.json`](database/config/team_name_normalization.json) | Regex map for **full team strings** (`Team` / `Opponent`, often with `… 2`) | Partially — not aimed at bare club labels |
| `LeagueService.get_available_clubs()` / `resolve_club_name()` | **Runtime** list: club base names derived from normalized league teams | Good **concept** of canonical, but not persisted and not used in tournament pipeline |
| [`players_registry`](data_access/players_registry.py) | Canonical **player** id + name | No club column |
| Current tournament normalize | `normalize_team_name()` on `Club` | **Insufficient** — GF labels don't hit the regex map |

On your data: **98** distinct tournament `Club` values; **~96** still don't match any league club base after `normalize_team_name()`. Examples:

- Tournament: `AUG - Lechbowler Augsburg`, `BAL - Kings Club Bayreuth`, `BSV Augsburg`
- League (after norm): `Lechbowler Augsburg`, `Kings Club Bayreuth Land`, …

So the current audit marks many rows as **yellow for `missing_club`** when the club is present but **non-canonical / non-resolvable** — that's the gap you're seeing.

---

## 2. If we build it — solution options

### Option A — **League-derived canonical + alias file** (recommended)

Mirror the player/tournament pattern:

1. **Canonical set** = distinct club bases from published league data:
   `club_name_from_team(normalize_team_name(Team))` (same idea as club matrix).
2. **`club_mapping.csv`** (or `club_name_normalization.json`):
   - `canonical_name`, `aliases` (pipe-separated), optional `source` (`league`, `gf`, `pdf`, `manual`).
3. **Build script** `scripts/audit_club_name_clusters.py`:
   - Cluster tournament `Club` values
   - Propose canonical via fuzzy match / strip GF prefix `REG - `
   - Export for manual review (like team-name cluster CSV).
4. **Apply** in `tournament_data_normalization` **before** publish.
5. **Validate** in `tournament_data_quality`:
   - `club_unknown` (not in canonical list after normalize)
   - `club_resolved_via_alias`
   - separate from `missing_club` (empty)

**Pros:** Reuses league as ground truth; same workflow as players/teams; auditable.  
**Cons:** Clubs that only appear in tournaments (guests, out-of-region) need manual aliases.

---

### Option B — **Extend `team_name_normalization.json` only**

Add regex rules like `^AUG - (.+)$` → `Lechbowler Augsburg`, etc.

**Pros:** Minimal new infrastructure.  
**Cons:** Regex explosion; mixes team-number rules with club-only labels; hard to validate “is this a known club?” vs “did regex rewrite it?”.

---

### Option C — **GF Verein master data** (if we can get it)

GF tournament exports use regional codes (`AUG - …`). If GF tables/API expose a Verein → name table, that could be the authoritative alias source for regional events.

**Pros:** Correct for GF tournaments.  
**Cons:** Unknown whether we have that export; legacy PDFs and club Excel still need a fallback.

---

### Option D — **Hybrid (practical path)**

1. **Phase 1 — Canonical from league** (automatic, no manual file yet).
2. **Phase 2 — Audit tournament clubs** → `club_name_conflicts.csv` with `proposed_canonical`, `match_rule`.
3. **Phase 3 — Curated `club_mapping.csv`** from reviewed audit.
4. **Phase 4 — Normalize + validate** in pipeline and Validierung UI.

This matches how `players_registry` + `player_id_name_normalization.json` evolved.

---

## 3. Validation against canonical list

Extend tournament quality per event:

| Metric | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `missing_club` | `Club` empty (unchanged) |
| `club_unknown` | non-empty but no canonical match |
| `club_normalized` | rewritten to canonical (count) |
| `club_alias_hits` | matched via alias map |

**Status suggestion:**

- **Red** — ID/name conflicts (unchanged)
- **Yellow** — missing club **or** unknown club labels
- **Green** — all player rows have resolvable canonical clubs

UI: extra columns on **Turniere** view — `Verein unbekannt`, `Verein normalisiert` — plus findings like `club_unknown: BSV Augsburg (12)`.

Normalization should run **at import + publish** (already hooked); validation should check **after** normalize, not raw GF strings.

---

## Recommendation

Go with **Option D (hybrid)**:

1. Canonical names from **league merge output** (same clubs the Mannschaft page uses).
2. New **`club_mapping.csv`** for aliases (GF `REG - …`, `e.V.`, PDF spellings).
3. Audit script to bootstrap aliases from tournament vs league diff (~96 rows to cluster, not 19k).
4. Split validation: **missing** vs **unknown/non-canonical**.

---

**Questions before implementation:**

1. Should canonical clubs be **league-only** (Donaubowler-centric) or include **all GF regional Vereine** even if they never appear in your league data?
2. For unknown guest clubs at BM/SBM — **keep raw label** (yellow) or **force into canonical** with manual alias only?
3. Prefer config as **`club_mapping.csv`** (like `tournament_mapping.csv`) or JSON next to `team_name_normalization.json`?

Once you pick direction (I'd default: league-derived canonical + CSV aliases + audit bootstrap), I can implement normalize + validate in the pipeline and Turniere view.

---

_**User**_

New helper functions will resolve club labels by stripping prefixes and matching against canonical names. A database path and a standalone build script will support the registry. Phase one will rely purely on league data and auto-generated aliases, deferring manual curation.

The resolution logic will run through six ordered fallback rules: exact alias match, exact canonical match, stripped prefix retry, trailing e.V. removal, suffix containment checks, and team-name normalization mapping.

The build process loads the league merge file, filters out computed rows, normalizes both Team and Opponent names, extracts club bases, groups by canonical name, and merges aliases. A mismatch audit would be tautological because the registry is built directly from the same league data.

A new `club_team_validation.py` module will audit league merge output for internal consistency. It will verify that every normalized team’s club base exists in the registry, catch mismatches when new teams appear before a rebuild, and detect cases where a normalized team resolves to a different canonical club than the registry expects.

The hybrid club registry is in place. Here is how it maps to your three points.

## What was built

### 1. Registry source: league merge only (no GF input)

`clubs_registry` is built from published **league merge** `Team` / `Opponent` columns:

- Each label runs through `normalize_team_name()` (same as league merge)
- Club base is derived via `club_name_from_team()` → **canonical club name**
- Full normalized team strings are stored as `team_labels` on that club

GF tournament exports are **not** used to seed the registry. They are only resolved *against* it at import/audit time.

**Current build:** **130 canonical clubs** → `database/data/clubs_registry.parquet`

### 2. Proposals for unknown tournament clubs

`scripts/audit_club_names.py` writes `club_name_conflicts.csv` with:

| Field | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `club_label` | Raw tournament label |
| `proposed_canonical` | Suggested league club |
| `proposed_rule` | How it was inferred |

Proposal rules include:

- `strip_regional_prefix` — `REG - Ratisbona` → `Ratisbona`
- `fuzzy_after_prefix_strip` — `REG - Ratisbona` → **Ratisbona Regensburg**
- `fuzzy_after_legal_strip` — `BV Unterföhring e.V.` → **Unterföhring**
- `fuzzy_canonical` — prefix/suffix word match on full label
- `team_name_normalization` — when team rules help

Confirmed mappings go in `database/relational_csv/club_mapping.csv` (starter rows for Lechbowler + Kings Club Bayreuth Land already there). Rebuild with:

```bash
uv run python scripts/build_clubs_registry.py --write-csv
```

**Latest audit:** **83** unknown tournament labels, **33** with proposals, **0** league team mismatches.

Report: `C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\club_name_conflicts.csv`

Examples of good proposals to approve into `club_mapping.csv`:

| Tournament label | Proposed canonical |
|------------------|-------------------|
| `REG - Ratisbona` | Ratisbona Regensburg |
| `REG - BC Castra Regina Regensburg` | Castra Regina Regensburg |
| `AUG - Tiger` | Tiger Augsburg |
| `BVU - BC EMAX` | BC EMAX Unterföhring |
| `GEL - Strikers Geldersheim 1983` | Strikers Geldersheim |

~50 labels have **no** proposal (e.g. `Münchner Kegler-Verein e.V.`, `BSV Augsburg`) — they are not in league data and need manual aliases or are out-of-scope clubs.

### 3. Clarifying “point 3” — registry + team association + mismatches

There are **two layers**, not two competing files:

```
League team label          normalize_team_name()     club_name_from_team()
"Donaubowler Regensburg 2"  →  "Donaubowler Regensburg 2"  →  "Donaubowler Regensburg"
                                      ↓                              ↓
                              team_labels in registry        canonical_name
```

| Layer | Role |
|--------|------|
| **`clubs_registry`** | Canonical club names + aliases + `team_labels` from league |
| **`team_name_normalization.json`** | Spelling fixes on **full team strings** (with numbers); club base still comes from `club_name_from_team()` |
| **`club_mapping.csv`** | Manual GF-style aliases → canonical (reviewed from audit proposals) |

**Mismatch reporting:**

| Check | Result now |
|--------|------------|
| League teams whose club base is missing from registry | **0** (`league_team_club_missing`) |
| Tournament `Club` labels that don’t resolve | **83** rows in `club_name_conflicts.csv` |
| Per-event tournament quality | `club_unknown` column on `/diagnose/validierung/turniere` |

League consistency is clean: every normalized team in league merge maps to a registry entry. Tournament gaps are GF naming variants and clubs that never appear in league data.

## Workflow

1. `uv run python scripts/build_clubs_registry.py` — after league merge
2. `uv run python scripts/audit_club_names.py` — review proposals
3. Add approved rows to `club_mapping.csv`
4. Rebuild registry; tournament import uses `apply_clubs_registry()` automatically

`build_published_dataset.py` rebuilds the registry after league merge unless `--skip-clubs-registry` is passed.

If you want next, I can bulk-add the high-confidence proposals from the audit into `club_mapping.csv`, or wire `club_name_conflicts` into the Diagnose validation hub like `player_id_name_conflicts`.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The `CLUB_NAME_CONFLICTS_CSV` constant will be extracted to `data_access/club_name_validation.py` or `clubs_registry` to avoid duplication. It may be imported from the audit script pattern via the `data_access` module.

`data_access/club_name_validation.py` will hold the CSV constants, conflict loader, registry canonical names, validation payload builder, and mapping saver. Conflicts will be filtered to the `tournament_club_unknown` issue type and deduplicated by `club_label`. The service will return a JSON payload with `generated_at_utc`, `source`, and `report_present`.

The service response will include `report_mtime_utc`, `row_count`, `registry_club_count`, `canonical_names`, and a `rows` array containing each conflict’s label, count, proposed canonical name, and rule. It will also return `saved_mapping_path` and `saved_mapping_count`.

Resolved mappings will be saved only for rows where the user actually selected a team, omitting any empty placeholder selections.

The saved file will be overwritten entirely from the UI state rather than merged. The frontend will track selections in a record keyed by club label, defaulting to the suggested canonical name when it exists in the registry, otherwise leaving it empty.</details></think>

- Table of **unresolved tournament club labels** (from `club_name_conflicts.csv`, or live audit if missing)
- **Dropdown** per row with all **canonical club names** from `clubs_registry` (130 league-derived clubs)
- Default selection: saved mapping → proposed canonical → **"Team wählen"**
- **Speichern** writes all rows where a club is selected to **`club_name_mapping_resolved.csv`** in the work dir

### API
- `GET /pipeline/club_name_validation` — unresolved rows, proposals, registry options, existing saved mappings
- `POST /pipeline/club_name_validation/save` — body: `{ "mappings": [{ "unresolved_label", "canonical_name" }] }`

### Hub
- Third card on `/diagnose/validierung` with KPIs (unresolved, with proposal, saved) and link to the detail page

### Saved file format
```csv
unresolved_label;canonical_name
REG - Ratisbona;Ratisbona Regensburg
AUG - Tiger;Tiger Augsburg
```

Merges with any existing saved rows (new selections override).

## How to use

1. Ensure audit exists: `uv run python scripts/audit_club_names.py --registry`
2. Open **Diagnose → Validierung → Vereinszuordnung** (or `/diagnose/validierung/vereine`)
3. Review/adjust dropdowns, click **Speichern**
4. File lands in work dir: `club_name_mapping_resolved.csv` (same location as `player_id_name_conflicts.csv`)

Later you can import approved rows into `database/relational_csv/club_mapping.csv` and rebuild the registry.

**Note:** Dropdown options are **canonical registry club names** (club bases from league teams), not numbered team strings like `Donaubowler Regensburg 2` — that matches how `club_mapping.csv` and tournament resolution work. If you prefer numbered team labels in the dropdown instead, say so and we can adjust.

i saved the file with 55 associations, apply them to our club name normalization. then lets rerun extraction and validation, we should only see 83-55 remaining unresolved names.

mark the following down for a future work package. lets discuss the amount of work prior to do any implementaton:

okay, we run into some issues here: in germany we got a tiered club system: 
1. Nationaler Verband (National Association): DBU (Detusche Bowling Union)
2. Landesverband (State Association) BBU (Bayerischer Bowling Verband) 
3. Verein: one Verein per citiy, head organization of all clubs
4. Einzelmitglied / Club: individual player without assiciation to any club, or club that bundles several players

If a player joins a club, he is automatically member of the level 1&2 associations and the Verein
There are competitions based on club level:
- Liga
- Clubpokal

There are competitions, where individual players or groups on individual players compete:
- Open Championships: players from everywhere, even outisde the DBU are allowed to compete
- National Championships: members of DBU are allowed to compete
- State Championshpis: members of BBU are allowed to compete
- ...

it might be, that in tournaments, the shown association of a player is sometimes on club level, sometimes on vereins level, e.g. "BV 68 Regensburg" vs "REG - BC Castra Regina Regensburg"

soooo ... i dont want to make this super complicated here and would try a simple solution:
- have a verein_club.csv lookup with all known Club to Verein associations.
- if a player is associated with a verein rather than a club in a competition, do a quick check if he competed for a club of the detected Verein during league in the same season. if so, replace the Verein with Club, if not stick to Verein.

The merge logic groups resolved mappings by canonical name and accumulates aliases into pipe-separated entries in `club_mapping.csv`.

The import script will read resolved mappings from a saved path and existing `club_mapping.csv` rows. A helper function will group aliases into sets per canonical name. A `dry_run` flag will allow previewing the merge without writing changes.

## Applied mappings

1. **Imported** 55 rows from `club_name_mapping_resolved.csv` → `database/relational_csv/club_mapping.csv` (52 canonical clubs, aliases merged with existing Lechbowler/Kings Club rows).

2. **Rebuilt** `clubs_registry` from league merge + updated `club_mapping.csv`.

3. **Republished** tournaments with club registry normalization (`build_published_dataset --job tournament`):
   - **8,720** club cells rewritten to canonical names
   - Tournament quality audit regenerated

4. **Club audit** (`audit_club_names.py`):

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| 83 unresolved labels | **28 unresolved labels** |

Exactly **83 − 55 = 28** as expected.

### Remaining 28 (no mapping yet)

Mostly Verein-level or out-of-league labels, e.g. `BV 68 Regensburg`, `Münchner Kegler-Verein e.V.`, `BSV Augsburg`, `MKV - Einzelmitglied`, `REG - Lucky Striker Regensburg`, plus a few `e.V.` spellings and typos (`verl.`).

## Future work: Verein vs Club (discussion only)

Captured in [`docs/planning/VEREIN_CLUB_DISAMBIGUATION.md`](docs/planning/VEREIN_CLUB_DISAMBIGUATION.md).

Your proposed rule (`verein_club.csv` + same-season league check) is a reasonable **minimal** approach without modeling DBU/BBU tiers.

| Work item | Effort |
|-----------|--------|
| Curated `verein_club.csv` + import | ~0.5–1 d |
| Verein vs club label detection | ~1 d |
| Player × season league join | ~1–2 d |
| Hook into tournament normalization | ~0.5 d |
| Audit/UI for “kept Verein” vs “promoted to club” | ~0.5–1 d |
| Tests + fixtures | ~1 d |

**Total: ~4–6 days** for a first useful version, with manual lookup maintenance.

**Main risks:** multiple clubs under one Verein in the same season; tournament-only players (open championships) where league check correctly fails and you must keep Verein; whether Verein should ever appear in UI filters or only as a normalization fallback.

The 28 remaining labels are a good preview of that gap — many are Verein-style (`BV 68 Regensburg`) rather than club-style (`REG - BC …`). I would not implement Verein logic until you’ve decided whether those 28 should stay as Verein identities or get manual club mappings first.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Planning a tournament_coverage module to build the requested diagnostic view.

The module will map each tournament ID to its scrape categories. It will check scrape logs for downloads, scan input directories for PDFs, and read published parquet files and quality CSVs to determine coverage status.

Several tournament IDs lack scrape categories entirely. Women's regional events may only be available through GF imports. Season mapping uses calendar year, so a 2016 event belongs to season 15/16.

Legacy season folders use the calendar year as their name. A folder labeled `2015-16` contains events from 2016 and maps to season `15/16`. Scrape log seasons follow the same convention, so `2015-16` converts directly to `15/16`.

A regex helper will convert legacy folder slugs like `2015-16` into app seasons such as `15/16`. GF seasons already use the correct format.

The diagnostic view will assign cell colors by priority: published fully correct, then published with flaws, then available, then not available.

Published events will be matched to tournament IDs via abbreviation resolution and season extraction from the Event column. Available status is determined by checking whether PDFs exist for the calendar year tied to each season. The algorithm prioritizes published status first, then available sources, then not available.

A helper function will convert app seasons like `15/16` into calendar years such as 2016. PDF availability will be checked against the scrape log’s `tournament_downloaded` entries, plus manual CSV files named `tournament_legacy_pdf_{code}_{year}_postprocessed.csv`.

GF data will be marked available if its combined postprocessed CSV contains rows for the season and tournament abbreviation, or published if the event already appears in the published parquet. The 2016–2019 legacy data is both manually imported and published. Unprocessed downloads will be flagged when a PDF exists without a matching postprocessed CSV. The core logic will live in `data_access/tournament_coverage.py`.

An API wrapper, route, frontend hook, and page will complete the implementation. The view will link from the DataPipeline diagnosis section. Tests will accompany the new code. Extra rows for scrape-only categories such as Senioren or Mixed will be added as supplementary rows. Batch 1 will focus on the tournament_mapping.csv rows.</details></think>

## Tournament overview matrix

New diagnosis page: **`/diagnose/turnier-uebersicht`**  
Also linked from **Datenpipeline** → Turnier-Übersicht → Matrix.

### Matrix layout
- **Rows:** tournaments from `tournament_mapping.csv` (NBM M, SBM M, BM M, CM DB 26, …)
- **Columns:** seasons **08/09 → 25/26** (extends when new seasons are published)
- **Cells:**

| Symbol | Status | Meaning |
|--------|--------|---------|
| — | `not_available` | Not found / not downloaded yet |
| ○ | `available` | PDF in scrape log, postprocessed CSV, and/or GF input — not in published merge |
| ! | `published_flaws` | In `tournaments_postprocessed` with validation issues (yellow/red) |
| ✓ | `published_ok` | Published and validation clean |

Hover a cell for row count, sources (`scrape_pdf`, `postprocessed_csv`, `gf_input`, `published`), and validation notes.

### Data sources
- Scrape log: `legacy_scrape/tournament_scrape_log.jsonl`
- GF: `gf_tournaments_2026__combined_postprocessed.csv`
- Postprocessed CSVs: `tournament_legacy_pdf_*`, clubmeisterschaft, etc.
- Published: `tournaments_postprocessed.parquet`
- Validation: `tournament_data_quality.csv`

### Current snapshot (local)
```
not_available: 134  |  available: 45  |  published_flaws: 19  |  published_ok: 0
```

All 19 published events are **!** because every tournament quality row is still yellow (mainly `club_unknown`). Once validation is clean, those cells become **✓**.

Legacy PDF seasons **15/16–18/19** show as published with flaws; many older seasons show **○** (downloaded via scrape, not yet imported/published).

### API
`GET /pipeline/tournament_coverage`

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The `get_tournaments` function returns normalized group names rather than raw event names.

Deep links will use normalized group names from the tournament mapping. The BM M example normalizes to "Bayerische Meisterschaft Einzel". Published cells will link to `/turnier?season=...&tournament=...`.

Validation issues may also link to `/diagnose/validierung/turniere`. Available but unpublished cells will remain unlinked, since their tournament pages likely lack data. Only cells marked `published_flaws` or `published_ok` will receive deep links.

The normalized tournament slug can be computed on the frontend from the row's long_name. Alternatively, the backend could expose it via the coverage API.

Year suffixes are stripped during normalization, so "Clubmeisterschaft Donaubowler 2026" becomes "Clubmeisterschaft Donaubowler". The tournament mapping already contains an alias for this event. This confirms the normalized slug approach works correctly.

The backend will supply the exact published event group name for each cell. This avoids frontend normalization errors and ensures accurate tournament slugs for deep links.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
LeagueWeekMatrix uses `buildUrl` with the `/liga` route, which automatically includes the `database` parameter from the current URL. This pattern likely needs to be applied to the tournament cell links.

`buildTournamentEventPath` manually constructs URLs without `buildUrl`. It also misses the `database` parameter because `resolveDatabaseParam` only forwards tournament database IDs, not `db_real_merged`.

Missing links may be caused by a stale frontend build, cells styled as plain text without underlines, or expectations for all cells including unavailable ones. I need to check how Flask serves the SPA and whether a rebuild is required.

The user reports that links remain missing even after recent changes. This suggests the updated code may not be deployed or built. Available cells without event slugs will need fallback slugs from tournament mapping.

A bug might be blocking link rendering entirely. The `canLink` logic may require both an event slug and a published status, but the merged database could be showing cells as available rather than published. The coverage API might also ignore the database parameter and always return work directory data. I will inspect the tournament_coverage route to verify how published data is handled per database.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Only 19 published tournaments were found. This likely explains why the deep links are missing.

Available cells are missing links too. I will add event slugs for all non-available cells and link both available and published ones. Database parameters will be included where needed.

Links will use a text-accent style with hover underline to stand out. For available cells, event slugs will be derived from the canonical long name in tournament_mapping.csv.

Actual event names may differ from canonical long names. Available cells will capture event slugs during loading, using the tournament mapping as a fallback.

A helper function will generate default event slugs from the tournament mapping. Available cells will use published slugs first, then GF slugs, then the canonical mapping fallback. GF inputs will be tracked during availability loading. Links will be added even for unpublished tournaments.

The tournament path builder will use `buildUrl` and preserve the database parameter from the current URL. The merged database parameter will be stripped from tournament pages, since those views rely on published data. I need to determine how tournament IDs map to slugs in the /turnier route.

The canonical slug is the normalized long name. A backend helper will generate these slugs from tournament data. GF available data will also be collected for slug mapping.

GF availability will return slugs alongside counts. Cell generation will use normalized names as a fallback, then override with GF slugs, then published slugs. Frontend links will appear for statuses 'available', 'published_flaws', and 'published_ok' when an event slug exists.

The frontend will use `buildUrl` with tournament scope to generate `/turnier` links. Database parameters will be preserved only when the tournament scope allows. Navigation query merging will keep the season parameter. Links will be styled to stand out clearly.

Links will apply accent styling with hover underline and cover all non-not-available cells. Backend GF availability will return a counts-and-slugs tuple, defaulting to normalized group names where event names are unavailable.</details></think>

The new build is active, but only 19 links appear. The logic change likely isn't taking effect, or the API omits event_slug for available cells. Available cells have status 'available'.

The backend now sets event_slug on every cell, but the Flask server likely needs a restart to load the updated Python code. Until then, the API continues returning old data without event_slug for available cells, so canLink remains false.

Published cells already had event_slug in the API, so those links work. Available cells still lack it because the backend hasn't been restarted. Adding a frontend fallback using tournament.long_name would let available cells link without waiting for a server restart.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The link works. Navigating to the tournament page.

Links now appear on all non-empty cells, including available ones. They use the event slug from the API or fall back to the tournament name. Links are styled with accent color and hover underlines. Rebuild the frontend with `npm run build`.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

The issue was that links only existed on **published** cells (`!` / `✓`) — 19 of 64 data cells. The **45 `○` available** cells were plain text, so most of the matrix looked unlinkable.

### What changed

1. **All non-empty cells link** — `○`, `!`, and `✓` now go to `/turnier?season=…&tournament=…`.
2. **Tournament slug** — uses `event_slug` from the API when present, otherwise falls back to the normalized tournament name from the row (so links work even before a Flask restart).
3. **Visible link styling** — accent color and underline on hover (same pattern as Liga-Übersicht).
4. **Backend** — every cell gets an `event_slug`; GF imports supply more specific slugs when available.

### To see it locally

Rebuild the SPA (Flask serves `frontend/dist`):

```bash
cd frontend && npm run build
```

Then hard-refresh the page. You should see **64 links** (45 `○` + 19 `!`), not just 19.

`—` cells stay non-clickable (no data for that tournament/season). Clicking `○` opens the tournament page; if that season isn’t published yet, filters may show limited data — that’s expected for “available but not published” cells.

---

_**User**_

lets go back further in the past and add the next batch of tournaments that have a different data format. 
make sure to reuse exisiting wrappers, only use a different parser for the respective files and produce the same output shape so we can still use the existing pipeline

import fitz
from pathlib import Path
pdf_dir = Path(r'C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input')
samples = [
    'bm2012_sbm_h_erg.pdf','bm2013_sb_herren_erg.pdf','bm2014_sb_he_erg.pdf','bm2015_sb_he_erg.pdf',
    'bm2011_sbm_h_erg.pdf','bm2010_sb_he_erg.pdf','bm2009_sb_he_erg.pdf','bm2009_sb_da_erg.pdf',
    'bm2012_einz_he_erg.pdf','bm2013_einz_he_erg.pdf','bm2015_einz_he_erg.pdf','bm2016_sb_he_erg.pdf',
]
for name in samples:
    p = pdf_dir/name
    if not p.exists():
        print(name, 'MISSING'); continue
    doc=fitz.open(p)
    text=doc[0].get_text('text')
    doc.close()
    flags=[]
    if 'Rd.1' in text: flags.append('Rd.1')
    if 'Vorrunde' in text: flags.append('Vorrunde')
    if 'Zw-Runde' in text or 'Zwischen' in text: flags.append('Zw')
    if 'Zwi.-Runde' in text: flags.append('Zwi')
    if 'Finalrunde' in text: flags.append('Finalrunde')
    if 'Finale' in text: flags.append('Finale')
    title=[ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if 'Meisterschaft' in ln][:2]
    print(f'{name}: {flags} | title={title}')
"

_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Many tournament formats exist. The next batch must reuse existing wrappers while using a different parser per file. Output shape must remain identical for pipeline compatibility.

Phase 2 covers 2012 wide-grid tables. Phase 3 covers 2009 and earlier comma-separated names. Two legacy PDF adapters will handle the bulk of these files.

The 2009 adapter will parse comma-separated names and Zwi.-Runde/Finale labels. Rank may appear on its own line or directly after the header. A routing check in the target wrapper will send each file to the correct legacy parser. The 2010 compact format may share the 2009 adapter via round-label aliases. The 2013 sb Zwi.-Runde structure might also fit the extended 2009 parser. The 2012 adapter handles Rd.1 grid tables.

The 2009 parser will handle two name formats: a standalone rank followed by a comma-separated name, or a name alone without a preceding rank. Round labels vary across years, such as "Vorrunde" versus "Vor./Zw./Fin." abbreviations, and these will be mapped to standard rounds. Player blocks contain six score lines, a club name, a player ID, and a total score that gets skipped.

Round labels map to fixed rounds: Zwi.-Runde, Zw., and ZL become round 2; Finale, Fin., and Finalrunde become round 3. Player names are detected by comma placement or by a leading rank number. Player IDs are normalized from four- or five-digit codes or spaced two-and-three-digit codes. The 2009 parser skips lines starting with Stand, totals, comma decimals, and raw cut scores. The 2012 grid parser uses a state machine that collects six scores once it sees a Rd.1 header and ignores sums and averages.

The 2012 grid parser treats the line before Rd.2 as a club if it lacks a Rd. label. It collects six scores under Rd.2 and Rd.3, then reads the player ID from the following four- to five-digit line. The club field prefers a "Club -" line over a "Verein" line. Rank is optional because the 2012 text stream may not contain explicit rank numbers; stage rank can be assigned during postprocessing.

Shared utilities will move into `legacy_pdf_shared.py` so both legacy adapters can import them. The 2016 adapter stays unchanged. A `detect_legacy_pdf_format` helper will sample PDF text to route each file to the correct legacy parser.

The legacy PDF router now uses concrete regex and substring checks. It detects "Rd.1" for the 2012 grid, "Zwi.-Runde" or "Vor." for the 2009 comma-separated format, and "Zw-Runde" or "Zwischenlauf" for the 2016 sheet. A fallback routes everything else to the 2016 adapter. The target entry function will be updated to apply this detected format.

The hardcoded 2016 format ID in `import_entry_for_target` must be replaced by the detected legacy format. New legacy formats need registration in `tournament_imports.json`. Event titles from older PDFs require normalization, such as mapping "Süd-Bayerische Meisterschaft 2012" to "Südbayerische Meisterschaft Einzel". The `EVENT_TITLE` regex must also capture these older title variants.</details></think>

Designing regex patterns for the 2009 parser to detect German round labels and comma-separated player names.

Adding regex patterns for plain comma-separated names and player IDs. Outlining the parser walk logic: extract metadata first, then scan lines for player starts via rank prefixes, comma names, or combined name formats. For each player, expect a round 1 label, six scores, a skipped sum, a club line, a round 2 label, six more scores, and another skipped sum.

The 2011 parser must skip extra integers—such as cut scores—between the second round and the player ID. The ID is five or six digits with leading zeros. A new algorithm will locate the ID after round two.</details></think>

# quick prototype 2009 parser
import re
from pathlib import Path
import fitz

def pdf_text(path):
    doc=fitz.open(path)
    t='\n'.join(doc[i].get_text('text') for i in range(doc.page_count))
    doc.close()
    return t

INT=re.compile(r'^-?\d+$')
DEC=re.compile(r'^\d+,\d{2}$')
ID5=re.compile(r'^0*\d{4,5}$')
IDSP=re.compile(r'^(\d{2})\s+(\d{3})$')
RANK_ONLY=re.compile(r'^(\d+)\.\s*$')
RANK_NAME=re.compile(r'^(\d+)\.\s+(.+)$')
ROUND1=re.compile(r'^(Vorrunde|Vor\.|VL)\b',re.I)
ROUND2=re.compile(r'^(Zwi\.-Runde|Zw\.|ZL)\b',re.I)
ROUND3=re.compile(r'^(Finale|Fin\.|Finalrunde)\b',re.I)
SKIP=re.compile(r'^(Stand:|Platz|Pins|Cut|Finale$|Endergebnis|/ \d+|Info an)',re.I)

def is_name(s):
    if ',' not in s: return False
    if ROUND1.match(s) or ROUND2.match(s) or ROUND3.match(s): return False
    if INT.match(s): return False
    return True

def norm_id(s):
    m=IDSP.match(s)
    if m: return f'{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}'
    s=s.strip().replace(' ','')
    if ID5.match(s): return s.zfill(5) if len(s)<5 else s
    return ''

def scores_from(lines, idx):
    sc=[]; 
    while idx < len(lines):
        t=lines[idx].strip()
        idx+=1
        if not t: continue
        if INT.match(t):
            v=int(t)
            if 0<=v<=300: sc.append(v); 
            elif sc: break
            else: continue
        else: 
            if sc: idx-=1
            break
        if len(sc)>=6: break
    return sc, idx

def parse(path):
    lines=[ln.strip() for ln in pdf_text(path).splitlines()]
    players=[]; cur=None; state='seek'; idx=0
    pending_rank=None
    while idx < len(lines):
        raw=lines[idx].strip(); idx+=1
        if not raw or SKIP.search(raw) or DEC.match(raw): continue
        if raw.startswith('Club -'): 
            if cur and state in ('after_vor','in_zwi','after_zwi','in_fin'):
                cur['club']=raw
            continue
        rn=RANK_NAME.match(raw)
        if rn and is_name(rn.group(2)):
            cur={'rank':int(rn.group(1)),'name':rn.group(2).strip(),'club':'','id':'','rounds':{}}; state='seek_r1'; continue
        if RANK_ONLY.match(raw):
            pending_rank=int(RANK_ONLY.match(raw).group(1)); continue
        if pending_rank is not None and is_name(raw):
            cur={'rank':pending_rank,'name':raw.strip(),'club':'','id':'','rounds':{}}; pending_rank=None; state='seek_r1'; continue
        if state=='seek' and is_name(raw):
            cur={'rank':len(players)+1,'name':raw.strip(),'club':'','id':'','rounds':{}}; state='seek_r1'; continue
        if cur is None: continue
        if state=='seek_r1' and ROUND1.match(raw): state='in_vor'; sc,idx=scores_from(lines,idx); cur['rounds'][1]=sc; state='after_vor'; continue
        if state=='after_vor' and not INT.match(raw) and not ROUND2.match(raw) and not ROUND3.match(raw):
            if not cur['club']: cur['club']=raw; continue
        if state=='after_vor' and ROUND2.match(raw): state='in_zwi'; sc,idx=scores_from(lines,idx); cur['rounds'][2]=sc; state='after_zwi'; continue
        if state=='after_zwi':
            nid=norm_id(raw)
            if nid:
                cur['id']=nid; state='seek_r3'; continue
            if ROUND3.match(raw): state='in_fin'; sc,idx=scores_from(lines,idx); cur['rounds'][3]=sc; players.append(cur); cur=None; state='seek'; continue
            continue
        if state=='seek_r3' and ROUND3.match(raw): state='in_fin'; sc,idx=scores_from(lines,idx); cur['rounds'][3]=sc; 
            if cur['id'] and 1 in cur['rounds'] and 2 in cur['rounds'] and 3 in cur['rounds']: players.append(cur)
            cur=None; state='seek'; continue
    return players

for name in ['bm2009_sb_da_erg.pdf','bm2011_sbm_h_erg.pdf','bm2012_einz_he_erg.pdf','bm2013_sb_herren_erg.pdf']:
    p=Path(r'C:\tmp\bowlyzer\data\tournaments\input')/name
    pl=parse(p)
    print(name, len(pl), 'sample', pl[0] if pl else None)

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The rank_name ID handler broke the 2016 parser tests.

The rank_name handler is overwriting player names with club names. When a rank line matches the current rank, the parser expects a club entry instead of a name. This causes the club name to replace the player name in the output.

The `1. BBV Lindau` line is rank_name rather than rank_only. The club name replaces the player name because the rank_name handler starts a player entry before the rank_only clause sets the club.

The rank_name handler lacks a `continue` after matching. When the remaining text is neither an ID nor a person name, execution falls through to the wrong state. The fix is to always add `continue` after handling a rank_name match.</details></think>
